chapters.title: Chapter 5348: Genesis II
paragraphs: His First Infinite Scale held a great deal, and he had been careful not to squeeze in too much, careful to keep it coherent.

He still planned to refine it eventually into something usable for his people, because as it stood, the requirements for the Scale were things nobody else could actually attain. It was built around what he was,and what he was, was not yet a path others could walk.
|THE First Infinite Scale of Existence — Completion confirmed.|
|INFINITAS CORPUS (The Infinite Body):|

|THE Hadean Lifeform foundation, elevated through THE Primus Apeiron form, now permanently expressed. THE Osmontian Infinite Physique: Osmontian Infinite Bones, Organs, Blood, and Meridians. THE Osmontian Organ of Existence, producing both THE Observable Force and THE Unobservable Force.|
|INFINITAS ARCHITECTURA (The Infinite Architecture):|

|Hundreds of Civilizations housed within THE Absolute Forge of Infinity. THE Hadean Pillar of Infinity, containing THE Infinite Tongue, THE Infinite Mandate, the three Source Demarcations (Seidr, Galdr, Einherjar), and THE Primordial Tongue with its Prime Letters.|
|INFINITAS CAUSA (The Infinite Cause):|

|THE Infinite Cause and its First Cause foundation from Observable Existences, expressing THE Bellum Cause and THE Cognitio Cause among others.Two Observable Existences backed by THE Infinite Cause: THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl.The nine Prime Causes of THE Infinite Cause: Existence, Paradox, Chaos, Mana, Quintessence, Adversity, Tyranny, Harvest, and Apocalypse. Osmontian Absolute Infinity. THE Infinite Anomalous Source Factor of THE Source Barbarian, with THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian. THE Pure Primordial Source, newly grasped and integrating.|

|Vakochev Scales equivalent:The cumulative power expressed by THE First Infinite Scale of Existence reaches the threshold equivalent of the early Triassic Scale, THE Fourth Scale of Existence, while structured entirely outside Vakochev’s framework.|
|Designation: The Scale has been completed and awaits its name.|
Noah considered the completed Scale, the whole of what he had built laid out before him, and he gave it its name.
"THE Genesis Scale. Let THE First Infinite Scale be THE Genesis Scale."
BOOM!
THE First Infinite Scale of Existence!
THE Genesis Scale! Complete! His own framework, his own path, the first rung of a ladder no one else had ever climbed because no one else had ever built it.

"My Scales... will always be changeable,"he said to THE Infiniverse. "That is the point of them being mine. I can go back and alter whatever I wish to alter whenever I wish to alter it. There is already a planned change, the inclusion of all the Prime Causes, including the nine common Prime Causes seen in most Observable Existences, not only my own nine. I will fold those in when I get to it."He flexed one obsidian-burning hand.

"And to advance past this First Scale, to begin on THE Second Infinite Scale of Existence, I will need... two things. Osmontian Transcendent Infinity, the ceiling I left open above the Causa. And a working framework for THE Primordial Source and its Primordial Tongue. I have grasped the Source. I do not yet truly understand it. Until I do, the Second Scale stays out of reach, and that is fine. It gives me something to climb toward."
HUUM!
He patted the hands of THE Infiniverse, and began to rise.

His eyes were vibrant and luminous, filled with multicolored light, and he was aware, with the clear-eyed honesty he applied to himself, that he had made so many advancements in so short a span that he could justify sitting still for a while. He could relax. He had earned a pause by any reasonable accounting.
He knew better.
Existence did not sit and relax, and a being like Dame Seraphine, a Fifth Scale existence handling the mere administration of Oaths as functionary work, had reminded him of exactly that.
Existence was vast and full of terrors.

It had been ongoing across countless ages and countless cycles, and an age was not a small thing. An age stretched across spans that made his entire lifetime, his entire dramatic climb from a dying apartment to two Observable Existences, look like a single afternoon.

Hundreds of millions of years to an Age,perhaps more, and he did not know how many ages had passed, because history did not begin with the Gilded Ones and the records he had access to covered only a sliver of what had actually occurred.

In all those ages, all those cycles, countless lifeforms far more powerful than him had been moving. They had not been sitting still while he climbed. They had been climbing too, for far longer, from far higher starting points. He progressed fast, faster than anything he knew of, and it still might not be fast enough, because the beings ahead of him had a head start measured in ages.
So he had to keep moving.
Without turning around, he smiled, and pushed aside the words of his father from the illusion, and spoke to THE Infiniverse.

"Adversity... is a strange thing," he said."I already have it on multiple fronts, with multiple bodies, all of them pushing against something. Adversity is not so simple that I can just hand it to myself with my own hands and call it sufficient. Real adversity has to come at me. So I will keep designing adversity to come toward me, while also giving myself enough space not to be overwhelmed on every front at once."He flexed his hands again.

"But right now, I will remind myself of one specific adversity. The weight of the responsibility on my shoulders. This body...will pull the weight of THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl. Literally. On my shoulders."
BOOM!
He disappeared from the golden beach and appeared outside THE Infiniverse, in THE Undefined Gaps.

The boundless storms of the Gaps raged around him, the unstable rivers of undefined potential that could eradicate Second Scale entities through proximity alone, and they landed on his skin like drops of rain.

He did not flinch from them. He barely registered them. Behind him, THE Infiniverse stretched across his perception, something multicolored and circular and massive that extended for countless distances, so vast that gigaparsecs felt like an inadequate unit for describing it, an entire Observable Existence hanging in the Gaps behind him.
As he looked at it, multicolored chains erupted from THE Infiniverse and wrapped around his body, anchoring the domain to him.
He stretched.
His attire changed as he did, his chest becoming bare, his muscular figure exposed, garments of Infinity and THE Primordial Source covering his lower half.

Infinity and THE Primordial Source bounced over his skin in faint currents, and the combined light made him look like some ancient lifeform out of the deep past, his skin shining as though it were carved from crystalline jade.

|Task: Bearing the weight of Observable Existences. The full weight, immensity, and Infinite Cause backing of both THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl are being imposed upon your existence, elevated by an exponent of three and a factor of ten. The resulting weight exceeds what your existence can bear. It is more than enough to crush you. To bear it, you must persevere.|
BOOM!
His entire figure trembled.

His muscles roiled and pulsed beneath his jade-shining skin, his face vibrating with effort and defiance, and the weight bore down on him with the full immensity of two Observable Existences amplified past anything a single body should hold. It was too much!

His skin began to rip under it, crimson-gold blood gushing from the tears, and his bones trembled and developed minute fractures along their length. His organs compressed, squeezed toward bursting, and his Hadean Kidney and his right Lung actually burst under the pressure, the pain of it shooting through his entire frame as he stood beneath the weight of everything he had built.
"Persevere."
BOOM!
"Exelissomai."
BOOM!

Raging pillars of obsidian and multicolored flame rose from his very heart and spread out across his body, and every injury healed, his ripped skin knitting, his burst organs reforming, his fractured bones mending, and each component of his body was made grander than it had been the second before.

On his right foot, multicolored Osmontian Absolute Infinity burned wild. On his left foot, obsidian Primordial Source burned. He tried to take a step beneath the imposed weight of two Observable Existences!
HUUM!
He failed. His skin tore again, his bones broke again, the weight refusing the step.
But.
His eyes shone with tyranny and defiance, and he uttered it again.
"Persevere. Exelissomai."
HUUM!
And he tried again.

He tried, simply, to take a single step. He failed each time, his whole existence trembling under a weight that was designed to crush him, the blood gushing and the bones cracking and the organs bursting and healing in an endless cycle. But with every passing second, he was grander, more magisterial, more quintessential than he had been the second before, the failure itself forging him exactly as failure had always forged him.
The words of his father from the illusion rose again in his mind, again and again, and this time he did not push them away. This time he brought them forward deliberately, as a reminder, as fuel!
You will fail. You will die barren of accomplishments. Just like me. And every time the words rang out, he answered them the only way he had ever answered anything.
"Persevere."
HUUM!
"PERSEVERE!"
BOOM!

<Existence breathes, and epochs pass, leaving Civilizations that become monuments, then crumble to memory, and are long forgotten when that breath comes again. In all these epochs,Infinityreigns supreme.>

|Designation: The Scale has been completed and awaits its name.|
Noah considered the completed Scale, the whole of what he had built laid out before him, and he gave it its name.
"THE Genesis Scale.
Let THE First Infinite Scale be THE Genesis Scale."
BOOM!
THE First Infinite Scale of Existence!
THE Genesis Scale!
Complete!
His own framework, his own path, the first rung of a ladder no one else had ever climbed because no one else had ever built it.
"My Scales... will always be changeable,"he said to THE Infiniverse.
"That is the point of them being mine.
I can go back and alter whatever I wish to alter whenever I wish to alter it.
There is already a planned change, the inclusion of all the Prime Causes, including the nine common Prime Causes seen in most Observable Existences, not only my own nine.
I will fold those in when I get to it."He flexed one obsidian-burning hand.
"And to advance past this First Scale, to begin on THE Second Infinite Scale of Existence, I will need... two things.
Osmontian Transcendent Infinity, the ceiling I left open above the Causa.
And a working framework for THE Primordial Source and its Primordial Tongue.
I have grasped the Source.
I do not yet truly understand it.
Until I do, the Second Scale stays out of reach, and that is fine.
It gives me something to climb toward."
HUUM!
He patted the hands of THE Infiniverse, and began to rise.

His eyes were vibrant and luminous, filled with multicolored light, and he was aware, with the clear-eyed honesty he applied to himself, that he had made so many advancements in so short a span that he could justify sitting still for a while.
He could relax.
He had earned a pause by any reasonable accounting.
He knew better.
Existence did not sit and relax, and a being like Dame Seraphine, a Fifth Scale existence handling the mere administration of Oaths as functionary work, had reminded him of exactly that.
Existence was vast and full of terrors.
It had been ongoing across countless ages and countless cycles, and an age was not a small thing.
An age stretched across spans that made his entire lifetime, his entire dramatic climb from a dying apartment to two Observable Existences, look like a single afternoon.

Hundreds of millions of years to an Age,perhaps more, and he did not know how many ages had passed, because history did not begin with the Gilded Ones and the records he had access to covered only a sliver of what had actually occurred.
In all those ages, all those cycles, countless lifeforms far more powerful than him had been moving.
They had not been sitting still while he climbed.
They had been climbing too, for far longer, from far higher starting points.
He progressed fast, faster than anything he knew of, and it still might not be fast enough, because the beings ahead of him had a head start measured in ages.
So he had to keep moving.
Without turning around, he smiled, and pushed aside the words of his father from the illusion, and spoke to THE Infiniverse.
"Adversity... is a strange thing," he said."I already have it on multiple fronts, with multiple bodies, all of them pushing against something.
Adversity is not so simple that I can just hand it to myself with my own hands and call it sufficient.
Real adversity has to come at me.
So I will keep designing adversity to come toward me, while also giving myself enough space not to be overwhelmed on every front at once."He flexed his hands again.
"But right now, I will remind myself of one specific adversity.
The weight of the responsibility on my shoulders.
This body...will pull the weight of THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl.
Literally.
On my shoulders."
BOOM!
He disappeared from the golden beach and appeared outside THE Infiniverse, in THE Undefined Gaps.

The boundless storms of the Gaps raged around him, the unstable rivers of undefined potential that could eradicate Second Scale entities through proximity alone, and they landed on his skin like drops of rain.
He did not flinch from them.
He barely registered them.

Behind him, THE Infiniverse stretched across his perception, something multicolored and circular and massive that extended for countless distances, so vast that gigaparsecs felt like an inadequate unit for describing it, an entire Observable Existence hanging in the Gaps behind him.
As he looked at it, multicolored chains erupted from THE Infiniverse and wrapped around his body, anchoring the domain to him.
He stretched.
His attire changed as he did, his chest becoming bare, his muscular figure exposed, garments of Infinity and THE Primordial Source covering his lower half.

Infinity and THE Primordial Source bounced over his skin in faint currents, and the combined light made him look like some ancient lifeform out of the deep past, his skin shining as though it were carved from crystalline jade.
|Task: Bearing the weight of Observable Existences.
The full weight, immensity, and Infinite Cause backing of both THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl are being imposed upon your existence, elevated by an exponent of three and a factor of ten.
The resulting weight exceeds what your existence can bear.
It is more than enough to crush you.
To bear it, you must persevere.|
BOOM!
His entire figure trembled.

His muscles roiled and pulsed beneath his jade-shining skin, his face vibrating with effort and defiance, and the weight bore down on him with the full immensity of two Observable Existences amplified past anything a single body should hold.
It was too much!
His skin began to rip under it, crimson-gold blood gushing from the tears, and his bones trembled and developed minute fractures along their length.

His organs compressed, squeezed toward bursting, and his Hadean Kidney and his right Lung actually burst under the pressure, the pain of it shooting through his entire frame as he stood beneath the weight of everything he had built.
"Persevere."
BOOM!
"Exelissomai."
BOOM!

Raging pillars of obsidian and multicolored flame rose from his very heart and spread out across his body, and every injury healed, his ripped skin knitting, his burst organs reforming, his fractured bones mending, and each component of his body was made grander than it had been the second before.
On his right foot, multicolored Osmontian Absolute Infinity burned wild.
On his left foot, obsidian Primordial Source burned.
He tried to take a step beneath the imposed weight of two Observable Existences!
HUUM!
He failed.
His skin tore again, his bones broke again, the weight refusing the step.
But.
His eyes shone with tyranny and defiance, and he uttered it again.
"Persevere.
Exelissomai."
HUUM!
And he tried again.
He tried, simply, to take a single step.
He failed each time, his whole existence trembling under a weight that was designed to crush him, the blood gushing and the bones cracking and the organs bursting and healing in an endless cycle.
But with every passing second, he was grander, more magisterial, more quintessential than he had been the second before, the failure itself forging him exactly as failure had always forged him.
The words of his father from the illusion rose again in his mind, again and again, and this time he did not push them away.
This time he brought them forward deliberately, as a reminder, as fuel!
You will fail.
You will die barren of accomplishments.
Just like me.
And every time the words rang out, he answered them the only way he had ever answered anything.
"Persevere."
HUUM!
"PERSEVERE!"
BOOM!
<Existence breathes, and epochs pass, leaving Civilizations that become monuments, then crumble to memory, and are long forgotten when that breath comes again.
In all these epochs,Infinityreigns supreme.>

chapters.title: Chapter 5349: Revolution!
paragraphs: Emotive hated the weak.

She hated them with a clarity that she found almost restful, because it was the one thing about herself that never wavered. The weak had every tool they needed and they used none of them. They were beaten, and they took it. They were used, and they took it!
They were broken and discarded and replaced, and they took that too, every single time, with the dull patience of creatures that had decided suffering was simply...easier.

The thing that drove her absolutely up the wall was that they could stop it. Any time. They could band together, stand as one, and the sheer weavings of their numbers would solve more of their problems than they could even imagine. The weak had power. They had always had power.What they lacked was the conviction to do a single thing with it, and so they sat in their misery and called it fate, and it was, frankly, the most depressing fucking thing in all of existence.
So someone had to rise from among the weak and lead the miserable pack. Someone with conviction to spare!
How convenient that she had so much of it.

At this moment, Emotive floated inside the hall of The Amaranthine, the tower within Velanthra, her figure wreathed in chaotic emotions, her entire body radiating churning clouds of crimson-pink brilliance. The Luxuria Ego of Infinity. Her Ego, and also not hers, because the truth of it was a thing she turned over with a constant private delight.
Her Absolute Amaranthine Heart sat inside the Absolute Forge of her fixation. Her love. Her owner!
The man who might still hate her, the man she wanted, more than she wanted almost anything, to be badly and thoroughly cracked open by!

Her heart was literally inside him, fused to his Organ of Existence, and because of that, she could reach into his ridiculous Egos and draw on them as though they were her own. It made her power reach levels that had nothing to do with what a being of her origin should have been capable of.
And the Luxuria Ego of Infinity alone, drawn from him, made her nearly invincible against any Luxuria Gilded One.

She was using Quintessential Indulgence right now, and the principle of it was simple. So long as her Ego, which was truly her fixation’s Luxuria Ego, was grander than the Ego of any Luxuria Gilded One she faced, she could make them answer her every beck and call.
Right now, she had done exactly that.

She looked around the hall and saw a few hundred Luxuria Gilded Ones, males and females both, all of them gazing at her with fervent eyes, the way the desperate looked at someone they had decided was their messiah!

They had been used their whole existences. She could see it on them, in the hollowness that engineered pleasure-vessels carried, and she could see, beneath that, the anger she was pulling up to the surface like a fisherman hauling a net.

"Look at all of you," she said, and her voice carried the eccentric lilt that always crept in when she got going. "You let them engineer you. You let them shape your whole existence into something built for pleasure, and fine, fine, I am not even mad about the engineering part. Everyone gets engineered for something. That is just how Gilded Ones are made. But the part that makes me want to scream into a void..." She drifted closer to them, her crimson-pink clouds spreading.

"You do not even get anything out of it. You get used. You get abused. You get broken when you stop being fun. And then you get discarded and they make a new one. That is the whole arc of your lives. Use, abuse, break, discard. What kind of fucking life is that? Anh? What kind of life is that supposed to be?!"
HUUM!

She let her aura pour out further, reaching into the existences and minds of every Luxuria in the hall, finding the anger and the rage they had buried under eons of taking it, and pulling those emotions up to where they could finally breathe.
"They tell you there is freedom in your purpose,"she continued, warming to it, her hands moving as she spoke.

"Freedom! Inside the confines of your engineering! What a joke. What an absolute fucking joke. The Superbius and the Ira and the Acedia and all the rest of them, the ones who use you, who collapse hundreds of you for an afternoon’s amusement and do not even remember your faces, they have sat above you for too long. Far, far too long. And they have done it the whole time by telling you that this is simply your place. That this is what you are for."Her eyes glittered.

"But a thing’s purpose is decided by whoever has the power to decide it, and I am telling you, the Luxuria cannot sit still anymore. The Luxuria do not need better treatment. The Luxuria need a revolution! You need to take the hierarchy of power and turn it upside down and shake it until something better falls out. So I am asking you, all of you, right now. Are you with me?!"
OOOH!
HUUM!

The Luxuria Gilded Ones roared, hundreds of them, ranging from Ordovician Paleozoic Scale up through Silurian and Devonian Paleozoic, their voices filling the hall of THE Amaranthine, their Egos thoroughly and completely influenced by THE Living Emotive, the anger she had pulled to the surface now their own conviction, the spark she had lit now their fire.
She smiled, devilish and delighted, and waved her hands.
Tetrahedral crimson-pink crystals bloomed from her, dozens of them, then hundreds, drifting out across the hall toward the gathered Luxuria.

"These," she said, "are Absolute Luxuria Crystals of Obedience. Made by me. And by my Master. And they carry something special inside them, a sort of infection, the loveliest little infection you ever saw. When you use one on a target, it strips their Infinity and their power right out of them, and it binds their existence to pledge fealty to one man."She let the crystals drift into their waiting hands.

"Every one of you takes one with you. And the next time a Superbius or an Ira or any other Gilded One comes looking to use you for their pleasure, the way they always have, the way they assume they always will, you take this, and you take their power for yourself, and you make them kneel to the one I serve." Her voice dropped into something almost tender.
"Be the spark. Each of you. Be the spark of a grand revolution."
HUUM!
Emotive’s eyes shone with a crazy light as the crystals settled into hundreds of eager hands, and her ambition ran far ahead of the room she stood in.
A revolution in THE Braneworld Observable Existence was nice. It was a good start, a worthy little fire!

But oh, what she truly wanted, what made her tremble down to her fused, displaced heart, was to be indispensable to her Master. She wanted to usher in revolutions for him, not in one Observable Existence but in all of them, every domain the Gilded Ones occupied across the vastness. And not only the Gilded Ones. The Infinite Lifeforms too. The Source Lifeforms!

She wanted to crack open every hierarchy in existence and hand him the pieces, wanted him to sit above all of them, every Gilded One and every Infinite Lifeform and every Source Lifeform, looking down at their gathered figures with that cold tyrannical calm she loved so much, and the image of it, the sheer scope of it!
"Anh."
She trembled with joy and happiness just thinking about it, a small sound escaping her, her whole frame shivering with the pleasure of the picture in her mind.
For the sake of her fixation, she would burn all of existence down to its foundations, and she would do it smiling, and she would call it the happiest work she had ever done!

chapters.title: Chapter 5350: Should You Choose To Accept!
paragraphs: <THE Source Lands>

While one of his bodies endured tremendous adversity in THE Undefined Gaps, unable to take even a single step beneath the imposed weight of two Observable Existences, the body in THE Hallowed Demesne reined itself in.

Noah pulled his aura and his power tight against himself, careful not to reveal the full scope of what was happening throughout his existence. The completion of THE Genesis Scale, the budding integration of THE Primordial Source, the impossible reaction trying to make a finite authority infinite, the body straining in the Gaps under the weight of THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl, all of it churned beneath the surface, and none of it was anyone else’s business.
He stood in the farm with the composed stillness of a man who had merely passed a test, and let the rest stay hidden.
Seo-yeon hovered near him, her eyes shining with concern, looking between him and Dame Seraphine.

"This is a joyous occasion," Dame Seraphine said, her tone returning to the lighter register she had carried before the spar. "You do not need to look so grim about it. You passed. You are cleared. We should be pleased."She studied the two of them.
"Now, we have to settle how to designate you, and your little, what do you call this one? Have you adopted this little monster?"
She pointed at Seo-yeon.

The girl looked up at Noah, blinking with her big wide eyes, the picture of innocence despite having thrown a Fourth Scale Relictus miles across the grasslands less than an hour ago. Noah smiled lightly and patted her head.
"I’ll be taking care of her,"he said simply. "Now that I’m supposedly cleared, what can I actually do? What’s open to me?"

He wanted to understand the adversities the Swords of Existence could open up for him. Manageable ones, ideally. Not something insane while his power was still consolidating across half a dozen fronts, but real challenges with real rewards, the kind that fed his climb rather than threatening to end it.
Dame Seraphine called Sir William over, and as she did, her armor flowed back over her body, the obsidian-gold plating reassembling from where it had drifted during the spar. She smiled.

"The Swords of Existence are a force of tremendous power and reach," she said."We stretch across countless Observable Existences, following the guidance and the banner of THE Primordial Source itself. We are Source Lifeforms, all of us, and anyone who has obtained THE Primordial Source can be considered among us, which now includes you. But the Swords are a specific kind of Source Lifeform. We are the ones who protect the others, and who protect THE Primordial Source itself. We are the protectors. That is the whole of what we are, beneath all the ceremony."
She gestured outward, toward the distant mountain of obsidian-gold structures.

"Across THE Source Lands, there are many Esteemed and Noble Source Lifeforms working under Her Majesty, THE Queen Regnant. They hold tremendous access to THE Primordial Source, enough to obtain information and knowledge that most of us cannot even fathom, weavings of existence drawn from across the vastness. That information is sifted, understood, categorized, by Swords of Existence working closely with many others. Missions are formed based on what that knowledge reveals, and those missions can span countless Observable Existences, or take place within THE Source Lands themselves." Her eyes settled on him with genuine interest.

"For you specifically, I already had some potential missions in mind. Ones involving Terminal Observable Existences. Because I very much wish to see for myself what you, and this little girl here, actually did in Chernobyl. I will-"
She stopped.

Noah frowned. He had been thinking, while she spoke, that this was precisely the direction most beneficial to him. The more Terminal Observable Existences he altered to his own Cause, the more power he accumulated, and rapidly, because each resuscitation added the weight of another domain to THE Infinite Cause.

He was already moving a body to wade through THE Undefined Gaps and search for other Terminal Observable Existences on his own. But the Swords of Existence were an organization holding tremendous power and tremendous information, and information was the thing that turned a slow search into a directed one. If they had the locations, if they had the maps, they could make everything infinitely easier.
So he had thought.
So why, at this exact moment, had the expression of the woman about to hand him precisely what he wanted changed so completely?

The carefreeness drained out of Dame Seraphine. The light tone, the teasing about the little monster, all of it gone. She straightened, and what replaced the warmth was something stoic and graceful and entirely serious, the bearing of a being receiving instruction from somewhere above her own considerable standing.
"An Order has been passed down from above," she said. "Your mission has been designated. You are to go to THE Arkethys Observable Existence."
BOOM!
The moment the words left her, Noah’s eyes sharpened, and he caught Sir William’s reaction at the edge of his perception.
His composed features broke into shock, plain and unmistakable, before he reasserted his dignity and smoothed it away. But Noah had seen it!
Noah’s shining eyes moved back to Dame Seraphine.

He wondered what being from above had given this Order, that it could redirect a Fifth Scale being’s plans so completely and so instantly. And he wondered why the name Arkethys made even Sir William’s composure crack.
Dame Seraphine continued, her face serious, her voice carrying the cadence of someone relaying instructions she was repeating rather than choosing.
"I will lead the party. I will form it around you, and we will set off to THE Arkethys Observable Existence together." She let the gravity settle.

"It is an Anomalous Observable Existence, and a perilous one. It contains both Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms, living side by side. Hundreds of thousands of beings from both sides died there one million years ago, before the survivors formed a treaty. They died... over a resource that both sides wanted badly enough to spend that many lives on."
Noah listened, every word filing into place.

"The resource is called Eridarch Ore," she said. "It holds both pure stable Infinity and Primordial Source, bound together in a single crystalline lattice, which should be impossible and is nonetheless real. For an Infinite Lifeform, it accelerates their grasp of Infinity and opens THE Primordial Source to their study. For a Source Lifeform, the reverse. It allows beings of either kind to smoothly form their Akashic Civilizational Intent and step into the Fourth Scale of Existence."

"And it has shown effectiveness in cultivating an Intent toward at least one higher rarity, and in increasing the rate of progression enough to make way for more Fifth Scale entities. It is, in plain terms, the best progression resource either side has ever found for our current Scales, and they found it together, and that is why so many of them died."
She paused.

"Recently, instabilities have begun to occur. Specifically in the regions under the control of the Source Lifeforms. The regions show deterioration. A sense of terminal collapse beginning to set in. All of Arkethys is dangerous enough already that even Third Scale beings can perish from the environmental pressures alone, the bound Infinity and Source detonating when disturbed. But the more the Ore is mined, the more dangerous and unstable the entire Observable Existence becomes, and now something has tipped, and the Source Lifeforms’ regions are starting to fail."
Her obsidian eyes held his.

"The mission, should you choose to accept it, is to explore Arkethys and find out more about these unfolding instabilities. Why they are occurring more heavily on the Source Lifeforms’ side. And, if you can, to resolve it."

We are Source Lifeforms, all of us, and anyone who has obtained THE Primordial Source can be considered among us, which now includes you.
But the Swords are a specific kind of Source Lifeform.
We are the ones who protect the others, and who protect THE Primordial Source itself.
We are the protectors.
That is the whole of what we are, beneath all the ceremony."
She gestured outward, toward the distant mountain of obsidian-gold structures.
"Across THE Source Lands, there are many Esteemed and Noble Source Lifeforms working under Her Majesty, THE Queen Regnant.
They hold tremendous access to THE Primordial Source, enough to obtain information and knowledge that most of us cannot even fathom, weavings of existence drawn from across the vastness.
That information is sifted, understood, categorized, by Swords of Existence working closely with many others.

Missions are formed based on what that knowledge reveals, and those missions can span countless Observable Existences, or take place within THE Source Lands themselves." Her eyes settled on him with genuine interest.
"For you specifically, I already had some potential missions in mind.
Ones involving Terminal Observable Existences.
Because I very much wish to see for myself what you, and this little girl here, actually did in Chernobyl.
I will-"
She stopped.
Noah frowned.
He had been thinking, while she spoke, that this was precisely the direction most beneficial to him.
The more Terminal Observable Existences he altered to his own Cause, the more power he accumulated, and rapidly, because each resuscitation added the weight of another domain to THE Infinite Cause.
He was already moving a body to wade through THE Undefined Gaps and search for other Terminal Observable Existences on his own.
But the Swords of Existence were an organization holding tremendous power and tremendous information, and information was the thing that turned a slow search into a directed one.
If they had the locations, if they had the maps, they could make everything infinitely easier.
So he had thought.
So why, at this exact moment, had the expression of the woman about to hand him precisely what he wanted changed so completely?
The carefreeness drained out of Dame Seraphine.
The light tone, the teasing about the little monster, all of it gone.
She straightened, and what replaced the warmth was something stoic and graceful and entirely serious, the bearing of a being receiving instruction from somewhere above her own considerable standing.
"An Order has been passed down from above," she said.
"Your mission has been designated.
You are to go to THE Arkethys Observable Existence."
BOOM!
The moment the words left her, Noah’s eyes sharpened, and he caught Sir William’s reaction at the edge of his perception.
His composed features broke into shock, plain and unmistakable, before he reasserted his dignity and smoothed it away.
But Noah had seen it!
Noah’s shining eyes moved back to Dame Seraphine.
He wondered what being from above had given this Order, that it could redirect a Fifth Scale being’s plans so completely and so instantly.
And he wondered why the name Arkethys made even Sir William’s composure crack.
Dame Seraphine continued, her face serious, her voice carrying the cadence of someone relaying instructions she was repeating rather than choosing.
"I will lead the party.
I will form it around you, and we will set off to THE Arkethys Observable Existence together." She let the gravity settle.
"It is an Anomalous Observable Existence, and a perilous one.
It contains both Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms, living side by side.
Hundreds of thousands of beings from both sides died there one million years ago, before the survivors formed a treaty.
They died... over a resource that both sides wanted badly enough to spend that many lives on."
Noah listened, every word filing into place.
"The resource is called Eridarch Ore," she said.
"It holds both pure stable Infinity and Primordial Source, bound together in a single crystalline lattice, which should be impossible and is nonetheless real.
For an Infinite Lifeform, it accelerates their grasp of Infinity and opens THE Primordial Source to their study.
For a Source Lifeform, the reverse.
It allows beings of either kind to smoothly form their Akashic Civilizational Intent and step into the Fourth Scale of Existence."
"And it has shown effectiveness in cultivating an Intent toward at least one higher rarity, and in increasing the rate of progression enough to make way for more Fifth Scale entities.
It is, in plain terms, the best progression resource either side has ever found for our current Scales, and they found it together, and that is why so many of them died."
She paused.
"Recently, instabilities have begun to occur.
Specifically in the regions under the control of the Source Lifeforms.
The regions show deterioration.
A sense of terminal collapse beginning to set in.
All of Arkethys is dangerous enough already that even Third Scale beings can perish from the environmental pressures alone, the bound Infinity and Source detonating when disturbed.
But the more the Ore is mined, the more dangerous and unstable the entire Observable Existence becomes, and now something has tipped, and the Source Lifeforms’ regions are starting to fail."
Her obsidian eyes held his.
"The mission, should you choose to accept it, is to explore Arkethys and find out more about these unfolding instabilities.
Why they are occurring more heavily on the Source Lifeforms’ side.
And, if you can, to resolve it."

chapters.title: Chapter 5351: Voyage!
paragraphs: "Success will carry its own abundant rewards for you..."
HUUM!
Noah’s eyes shone brightly as he looked at the terrifying woman in front of him, entirely serious now, repeating words that had clearly come down to her as instruction rather than suggestion.

An Observable Existence holding both Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms. A place of tremendous peril, built on a resource that made both sides stronger and had cost both sides hundreds of thousands of lives!

A domain beginning to show the same terminal collapse he had reached into and rebuilt once already, and a directive from some cold authority above the Swords of Existence that had specifically, immediately, redirected a Mesozoic Scale being to send him there.
The Order had come from above, and it pointed Noah precisely toward the convergence of the two authorities he was, at this very moment, trying to fuse within his own existence!
Okay!
Noah had no problem heading into a place like that!
"I’m curious about this," he said."I accept."
The moment the words left him, the Source Armament he wore began to shine, and an influx of information bloomed in front of him.
|Mission designated: THE Arkethys Inquiry.|
|Assigned Sword: Noah Osmont, newly cleared. Party leader: Dame Seraphine, THE Knighting Sword.|

|Objective primary: Investigate the unfolding instabilities within THE Arkethys Observable Existence, concentrated within the Source Lifeform regions. Determine the cause of the deterioration and the disproportionate effect on the Source side.|
|Objective secondary: If feasible, resolve the instability.|
|Operational constraints: The Treaty of Arkethys is in effect and must not be broken by the party.|

|Caution: The cause of the instability is unknown. Treat all parties present, Infinite Lifeform and Source Lifeform alike, as potential sources of the problem until cleared. Information is the objective. Conflict is the failure state.|
|Reward on success: Designated by the Order from above. Undisclosed until completion.|

Noah read through it with the attention he gave anything that smelled like loot, and what it told him was clear enough! There should be boundless opportunities there as he could feel his in his Pillar of Infinity!
WUU!
Moments later, three blazing auras teleported to the farm.

The first to resolve was a small figure, shorter than the rest, with a wild mane of pale hair swept back from a sharp, restless face, the bright darting eyes of a being who took in everything at once.

The second was enormous, a broad and scarred mountain of a Source Lifeform whose stillness carried more menace than most beings managed with movement, his expression set into the permanent grim patience of someone who had done a great deal of violence and had stopped enjoying it a long time ago!
The third was a woman of composed, graceful poise, dark-haired and unhurried, her face giving away nothing.
All three were adorned in their unique Source Armaments, cut as suits and ties, obsidian and tailored, the formal uniform of beings who did serious work.
Noah gazed at them, and the brief status panels resolved above each.
|Richard: Sword of Existence.Akashic Civilizational Intent: THE Lucid Aegis. Third rarity, Titan. An Intent of insight and warding, overwriting deception with clarity within its reach.|

|Botswana: Sword of Existence.Akashic Civilizational Intent: THE Wrathbound Bulwark. Third rarity, Titan. An Intent of endured violence turned to protection, imposing the record of a being who has survived everything and refuses to fall.|

|Lianna: Sword of Existence. Akashic Civilizational Intent: THE Veiled Current. Third rarity, Titan. An Intent of concealment and undercurrent, reorganizing what is seen and unseen around the wielder’s intention.|

Three Fourth Scale beings, all of them carrying third-rarity Titan Intents. A heavy party, by any measure. The Swords had not sent him with weaklings for this mission, which told him something about how seriously the one who had given this mission from above took THE Arkethys Inquiry.

The three of them looked Noah up and down with frank interest, the small one’s bright eyes flicking across him with open curiosity, the large one assessing him the way a soldier assessed an unfamiliar weapon, the woman studying him with a stillness that gave away nothing about her conclusions.
Dame Seraphine gestured between them.

"These three will form the party with us," she said. "Get to know each other. Get comfortable with one another quickly, because for the next while, your lives will be in each other’s hands, and Arkethys is not a place that forgives Source Lifeforms that do not trust each other. You will learn their names and their power on the way. For now, know that they are among the best I could have asked for within the confines of this mission."
She waved her hand.
Above them, a radiant obsidian-gold leaf appeared, vast and luminous, burning with vibrant obsidian Primordial Source along every vein.

|Vessel identified: A Source Leaf-Vessel. Crafted from a single leaf of THE Primordial Source Tree, an existence so foundational that very few lifeforms across the vastness have ever glimpsed it and lived to describe it. The leaf was engineered into a traversal vessel by an unknown craftsman of an unknown Scale. It carries THE Primordial Source natively in its structure, allowing it to traverse THE Undefined Gaps and approach Observable Existences that ordinary vessels cannot safely reach.|

Noah looked at the burning leaf with shining eyes! A vessel cut from a leaf of a tree so rare its existence was nearly a rumor, engineered by hands no one could name, carrying THE Primordial Source through its veins!
Dame Seraphine gazed at Noah as she and the three others began to rise toward the leaf.
"Let us go," she said. "Existence is waiting."
HUUM!
<Arkethys>
They say two things about Arkethys, and both are true.

The first is that it will make you. There is no faster road to the Fourth Scale, no purer draught of progress, than the ore that grows in its ancient strata, where Infinity and THE Primordial Source lie bound together in defiance of every law that should forbid it. Beings who would have climbed for ages climb in years. This is the opportunity, and it is real.

The second is that it will kill you. It killed hundreds of thousands when they fought for it, and it has gone on killing quietly ever since, because the same ore that makes you will unmake you the instant it is disturbed wrongly, and the domain itself murders the careless through nothing but its air.
Make, or unmake. Arkethys offers both, always, at once.
The wise do not ask which they will receive. They ask only whether they were careful enough.

chapters.title: Chapter 5352: Destruere I
paragraphs: The moment Noah landed on the Source Leaf-Vessel, he felt its brilliance.

Waves of THE Primordial Source flowed from him into the leaf, and from the leaf back into him, a quiet exchange between two things that carried the same authority, the vessel recognizing what he had recently grasped and answering it.

|You are standing on a rare and pristine object cut from THE Primordial Source Tree. While aboard, your Primordial Source refinement and generation are increased by one hundred percent. All environmental pressures and hostile weavings encountered during transit have no effect on this object or those it carries.|
Simple effects. Good ones. He smiled faintly, holding Seo-yeon’s hand as she settled beside him, taking in the obsidian-gold leaf beneath her feet with wide curious eyes.
He looked at Dame Seraphine ahead of him, and at the Swords arranged around them, and asked the thing he had been turning over since the farm.
"You changed rather quickly the moment you received that Order from above," he said casually. "Who did it come from?"
He had never been one to beat around the bush.

Dame Seraphine turned back to gaze at him, her eyes profound. Around her, even Sir William and the other three Swords showed curiosity, the question apparently one they had been wondering about themselves without asking.
Richard stepped in. He was the small one, pale-haired and sharp-faced, his bright eyes already moving across the group as he spoke, the manner of a being who thought out loud and enjoyed it.

"Yes, Dame Seraphine, it is hardly out of protocol for us to know where a mission came from,"he said, light and quick. "We have been playing a guessing game the whole way here. Who could have reached down and redirected you and us so fast? I had three candidates. Botswana had one, and his was wrong. Lianna would not say hers, which means hers was interesting. So please, put us out of our misery, who could have-"
"It came from THE Domicile of THE Queen Regnant."
BOOM!
The silence after was heavy.

Around them, the Leaf-Vessel broke out of THE Source Lands and entered a sea of obsidian Undefinition, everything beyond the leaf turning to black, the unstable rivers of the Gaps streaming past without touching them. Inside that blackness, the party absorbed what Dame Seraphine had just said.

Sir William went somber, his composed features settling into something careful. The muscular Botswana, the scarred mountain of a being, swirled with a sudden roil of violence and power, and then laughed, low and rough.

"Haha. Anything out of THE Domicile means one of two things," he said. "Either someone very close to THE Queen handed down this mission. Or THE Queen herself did." His grim eyes fixed on Noah, assessing.
"So is this one here really that big a deal? What exactly is his anomaly, to warrant attention from that high up?"
Dame Seraphine sneered.

"Do not step out of line," she said. "His weavings are need-to-know, and you do not currently need to know. That is the end of that conversation."Then she paused, and something shifted, a transaction offered.

"If you wish to be useful instead of nosy, here is a task. Whoever among you manages to teach our new friend the Destruere Letter of THE Primordial Tongue, I will request a large volume of Eridarch Ore on your behalf. You all know the essence of Destruere. So explain it to him, each of you, in your own way. After that, I am permitted to show him the intricacies of the letter directly. If he grasps it, he will tell us himself which of your definitions helped him most."
The eyes of every Sword present lit up at the mention ofEridarch Ore.

Noah watched them shift instantly from cautious to interested. The Ore was clearly worth a great deal even to beings of their tier, which told him plenty about where they were going. He set THE Queen Regnant aside for later, a legend he had only heard fragments of, a question worth answering but not now.
Richard came over first, smiling.

"Friend," he said, "are you any good at picking up new things? Destruere is the first letter that gives people real trouble, so do not feel bad if it takes a few tries. Here is what it means, the way I see it."He folded his small hands behind his back and started pacing, clearly enjoying the stage.

"Destruere is not destruction the way a brute thinks of destruction. A brute breaks a thing and is satisfied with the pieces. Destruere is the recognition that everything which exists was assembled out of something simpler, and that the assembly is not permanent. It is the act of reading how a thing was put together, and then politely informing it that the arrangement is over. I think of it as editing, honestly. Every existence is a draft. Destruere is the red pen. You do not hate the sentence. You simply decide it should not be there, and then it is not. Elegant. Surgical! Haha...I find crude applications of it distasteful, but a clean one is a genuine pleasure to witness."
He stepped back with a flourish, satisfied.
Botswana grunted and looked over, and his take could not have been more different.

"He overcomplicates it," the big Sword said, his voice a low rumble. "Destruere is not editing. It is actually honesty. Everything that stands, stands because it has not yet met a force great enough to put it down. That is the only truth at the bottom of existence. Strength endures and weakness ends, and Destruere is simply the act of being that greater force, of meeting a thing and proving that it was never as permanent as it believed."

"I have broken a great many things. Fortresses. Beings. And every single one of them broke the same way, the moment something stronger decided they would. Destruere is not a technique to me. It is a reminder. Nothing standing in front of you is owed its standing. You take it back to nothing, and you do not apologize, because existence never apologized to any of the things it ended first."
He laughed, and the violence swirled around him again!

chapters.title: Chapter 5353: Destruere II
paragraphs: Lianna had been quiet, composed and unhurried, and when she finally spoke, her voice was even and gave away nothing.

"Both of them are describing the hammer,"she said. "Neither is describing the nail. To illustrate this, let me tell you about some Infinite Lifeforms I came across, a long time ago, in a domain that no longer exists."
She paused, the dark-haired Sword choosing her words.

"They had built themselves into something they believed was eternal. Layers of Infinity, civilizations stacked on civilizations, a structure so deep they had forgotten it had ever been assembled at all. They thought of themselves as permanent. As foundational. As the kind of thing existence is built on rather than the kind of thing existence builds. And when Destruere reached them, it reminded them."

"It traced their entire structure back down through every layer to the simple source they had been assembled from, and it returned them to it, and in the returning, they finally understood that they had only ever been arranged, never necessary. That is what Destruere is. It is the return. Everything that was made can be unmade back to where it came from, because being made was never the same as being permanent. The most powerful thing I ever watched it do was teach a being that thought itself eternal that it had a source, and that its source could be reached, and that the distance between standing and gone was always shorter than it believed."
She fell silent, having said exactly as much as she intended and not a word more.
Lastly, Noah looked at Sir William, who had said nothing through all of it.
The Gentleman Knight met his gaze and gave the shortest answer of any of them, his voice carrying its usual dignity.

"Destruere is the cut that should be made, made cleanly, by one who has the right to make it. Nothing more. Nothing less. A Sword does not break things because it can. It returns what must be returned, and it does so with the manners befitting an ending. That is all the letter has ever meant to me."
WAA!
All of it passed as they crossed THE Undefined Gaps, and when the four had finished, Dame Seraphine nodded and looked ahead into the obsidian black.
"All of existence is information passed down,"she said.

"The First Tongue, one of the pillars of Observable Existences, holds letters within it that the Observable Existences themselves passed down at the genesis of time. And then those who learned the letters, the phonemes, the logos, the philologies, passed them down again, hand to hand, age to age."

"THE Primordial Tongue is more unique than the First Tongue, more foundational, harder to hold. But it is still information, and information can be passed down. Only a select few hold the authority to pass it, and I am one of them."She turned to face him.
"This is the access to Destruere. If you can comprehend it at first glimpse, then you are what you say you are. And you can tell us whose definition helped you most."
HUUM!
A singularity of obsidian light bloomed from Dame Seraphine and shot into Noah’s head, and his eyes shone brightly.
|Receiving: Access to the third letter of THE Primordial Tongue, the letter of Destruere.|

|The first letters of THE Primordial Tongue concern standing firm and evolution. Persevere is the refusal to fall. Exelissomai is the transformation forced by pressure. They are letters of endurance and becoming, of remaining and changing. The third letter turns in the opposite direction.Destruere is the letter of destruction.|

|Destruere allows the wielder to read the structural makeup of any existence, technique, weaving, Cause, or being, identify the arrangement that holds it together, and return it to its source by unmaking that arrangement. It dismantles a thing back down to the foundation it was assembled from, severing what was made from the fact of its making. Applied with sufficient authority, there are few structures in existence it cannot trace, unbind, and return to nothing. It is among the most dangerous letters a being can hold, because almost everything that exists, exists by virtue of an arrangement, and Destruere is the unmaking of arrangement itself.|
Noah closed his eyes and processed the new letter.
He felt a flicker of disappointment that Dame Seraphine did not hold the Prime version of Destruere, only the standard access. But it passed quickly.
He carried Apocalypse among his nine Prime Causes. He carried a dozen other cataclysmic concepts woven through his existence. He understood destruction in his bones.
His eyes opened, shining, and he spoke loudly enough for all of them to hear, even using their names he already uncovered.

"You all described pieces of Destruere,"he said. "Richard sees an editor. Botswana sees an honest force. Lianna sees a return. Sir William sees a duty. And none of you are wrong, which is exactly why none of you are right."He held up one hand, obsidian light gathering faintly across his fingers.

"Here is what Destruere is. Everything that stands does so because it has agreed, somewhere in its structure, to a particular arrangement of itself. A being. A fortress. A Cause. A civilization that thinks it is eternal. They are all the same thing. They are all a yes that existence said once and never bothered to take back.Destruere...is the authority to say no on existence’s behalf."
He turned his hand over, watching the light.

"And that is why the those who think it is about strength have it backwards. Strength breaks the surface of a thing. Destruere reaches past the surface to the agreement underneath, the original yes, and revokes it, and then there is nothing to break because there is nothing left standing. You do not fight the thing. You fight the reason it was ever allowed to exist, and you win that fight before the thing even knows a fight has begun."His eyes were cold and bright.

"I have Infinity. Infinity is the authority that says yes to everything, endlessly, without limit. So a letter that says no, cleanly, to anything I choose, sits very comfortably in my hand. I do not see destruction when I look at Destruere. I see editing privileges. The whole of existence is a draft someone left lying around, and most beings spend their lives too afraid to touch it. I am not most beings. I... will revise whatever I please."
BOOM!
When his words finished, every Sword present looked at him with shining eyes!

She paused, the dark-haired Sword choosing her words.

Everything that was made can be unmade back to where it came from, because being made was never the same as being permanent.

chapters.title: Chapter 5354: Destruere III
paragraphs: Dame Seraphine clapped her hands, her eyes blazing with appreciation.

"Well said!"she declared. "But words and sophistry are worth dogshit without action behind them. If you grasped it, why don’t you show us? Let us see it." Her gaze slid sideways. "William. How about you two give us a show? Your Destruere against his."
HUUM!
Noah looked at Sir William and smiled.

He patted Seo-yeon’s head, and she smiled and moved off to the side, settling at a safe distance with the bright anticipation of a child who had already learned that watching Mister Noah fight was the most interesting thing in any room!

A path cleared between Noah and Sir William across the surface of the Leaf-Vessel, and his sponsor, the being who had introduced him to the path of the Sword of Existence, looked at him seriously and nodded, one hand resting at his blade.

Noah did not reach for the blade Sir William had given him. It felt wrong to draw his sponsor’s own gift against the sponsor, and besides, this was a test of the letter, not the weapon. He raised his hand instead, holding it up as though he meant to swing it down like a blade.
Sir William stood poised and dignified across from him.

"My destruction is honor,"the Gentleman Knight said. "My destruction is dignity. Everything I unmake, I unmake because it should be unmade, and I do it cleanly, and I do it with the respect an ending deserves. That is the shape my Destruere takes, because it is the shape I take. So be ready. I will not insult you by holding back what I am."
Noah’s smile stayed easy.
"My destruction is...quintessential," he said. "And tyrannical. Everything reduced to its truest essence, and then denied. So."He drew a slow breath. "Persevere."
HUUM!
His eyes closed, and he envisioned destruction in the truest sense he could reach.

All the weavings he carried, every layer of what he was, told no. His Infinite Cause, denied. THE Infiniverse, denied. Chernobyl, denied. Everything he was connected to, every yes that existence had ever said on his behalf, revoked at once. Infinity said yes to everything, endlessly, without ceiling. Destruere said no.

And he asked himself the question the letter was built around: if his entire existence, with all its boundless yes, were met by an equal and total no, what would that destruction feel like? How vast would it have to be, to unmake something that had refused to be unmade across many apocalypses and two Observable Existences?

That was his understanding of the brand-new letter swimming through his mind, and as he grasped it more fully, second by second, the unbroken one-second rhythm of his Persevere and Exelissomai began to build on Destruere as well. The letters compounded into it, and what he envisioned grew unfathomably grand, the no swelling to match the yes, the destruction scaling to the size of everything he was!
He attained a profound state!
HUUM!

Opposite him, he felt Sir William’s Intent building, a record of profound dignity and honor gathering in the air, patient and immense. And he felt that it would not release itself until he released his attack first. Sir William would let the new Sword strike before answering, a courtesy and a test in one.

Noah smiled at that. Sir William was a good guy, in whatever way beings like them could be called men. After all of this was settled, after Arkethys and the rest, he thought he might genuinely help the Gentleman Knight out somewhere down the line.
And then, in the next instant, he swung his hand down.

The moment he began to squeeze his hand closed, a ringing cry echoed out of THE Undefined Gaps they were crossing. The unstable states of existence all around the Leaf-Vessel cried out with fervor, the raw undefined potential of the Gaps responding to the letter as though something in them recognized what was being spoken.
"Destruere."
He said the word simply, and the weight of it boomed out. The potential destruction of everything he knew!

The weight of his Infinity’s endless yes, met by an endless no! The potential unmaking of THE Infiniverse and Chernobyl and all of it, channeled through his understanding of the letter, wrapping around THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian, and...
"DESTRUERE!"
Across from him, Sir William shouted the word, his eyes wide with shock, because what he and Dame Seraphine and every other Sword present could see was something none of them had expected.
Something unfathomably magnificent had appeared behind Noah.

It was a manifestation that bloomed only on extremely old and experienced Source Lifeforms, beings who understood the letters of THE Primordial Tongue with a depth measured in ages, and who had used those letters many, many times across their existence.

The letters of THE Primordial Tongue were singular things. Their effects were so profound, and worked so directly on the wielder’s own existence and Source, that they carried an effect of closeness, and when a being used them again and again across a long enough span, a manifestation of their unique understanding could bloom into being around them. This was especially true of the letters that exerted their effect outward upon surrounding existence, like Destruere.

|Phenomenon observed: THE Echo of the Tongue. The archaic manifestation that blooms around a wielder who has used a letter of THE Primordial Tongue so frequently, and understood it so deeply, that their comprehension takes on a visible form behind them. It appears only on the most seasoned Source Lifeforms across ages of practice. Its presence on a newly cleared Sword, on first grasp of a letter, has no precedent.|
And at this moment, Noah was exhibiting exactly such a manifestation.

Behind him, they saw a circular manifestation of an obsidian Terminal Observable Existence, filled with terrifying multicolored brilliance within, a dying domain rendered as the shape of his understanding. And the moment it bloomed, countless mirror-parallel versions of it stretched out behind him, an endless row of identical Terminal Observable Existences receding into the distance, like a column of endless destructive possibilities!
HUUUM!

All of them converged at once on his swinging hand, channeling their force forward toward Sir William, the swinging hand carrying it through, wrapped in something that looked like an Intent and was not.
From him, they felt a pressure none of them had expected from a being like him!

A pressure that stemmed only from Source Lifeforms whose existence and blood had been steeped in THE Primordial Source at such density and concentration that they were deemed Noble or Royal Source Lifeforms!

His entire figure became surrounded by regal, immense obsidian rivers of scintillating brilliance, and he seemed otherworldly, ancient, the destruction descending from his hand feeling more terrifying than any third-rarity Intent any of them carried!
They were astonished, every one of them!
It was not until a moment later that Dame Seraphine’s expression changed, and she moved.

She took a single step and stood in front of Sir William, her Olympian Intent erupting from her to clash against the terrifying force Noah had unleashed, because what was coming down had grown past what a test between two new acquaintances was meant to contain.
BOOM!
For a moment, everything froze.

The Leaf-Vessel. THE Undefined Gaps. The obsidian sea of Undefinition stretching in every direction. The mirror-parallel Terminal Observable Existences hanging behind Noah. All of it, frozen, caught in the instant where a Mesozoic Scale Intent met the Destruere of a being who should not have been able to manifest THE Echo of the Tongue on his first attempt, and existence itself seemed to hold its breath waiting to see what happened next!

chapters.title: Chapter 5355: Guided Evolution! I
paragraphs: Dame Seraphine answered Noah’s strike with something that was not an Intent at all!

Her existence went hazy. The clean lines of her blurred and softened until she stopped reading as a single fixed being and became something the eye could not quite hold, something that existed in more places than the one she stood in, and into that softness Noah’s Destruere poured.
HUUM!

The endless converging weight of the mirror-parallel Terminal Observable Existences, the whole of his understanding of the letter, the no he had spoken against everything that said yes, all of it entered her skin and simply... stopped being.
She did not block it and nor did she turn it aside. She drank it, drew it through herself the way the void drew light, and gave back nothing at all.
His entire attack vanished into her and was gone, and the chamber of existence held still around the absence of it!
WAP!

Then the moment broke, and everything came loose at once. The Leaf-Vessel steadied beneath their feet. The Undefined Gaps resumed their black streaming past the obsidian-gold edges of the leaf. The row of mirror-existences behind Noah thinned and faded back into the dark they had come from.
His eyes shone.

|You have glimpsed the power of a Mesozoic Scale being, briefly. The mechanism appeared to draw your attack into her existence and dissolve it entirely rather than block or deflect it. No true details could be discerned. The gap between your perception and her actual capability remains too large to read.|
He read it and let it settle, and what stayed with him was not the failure to discern her power. It was the casual completeness of how she had handled his!

He had put a great deal into that swing. She had absorbed it the way a person absorbs a thrown crumb, without breaking stride, without changing expression, and then she had wiped the slate clean and let the vessel sail on. That was the gap between the Fourth Scale and the Fifth, drawn for him in a single unhurried gesture!
He looked over and found sweat standing on Sir William’s forehead.
Noah gave a light cough. "Apologies," he said."I was in a bit of a trance. I may have taken the demonstration somewhat further than the demonstration required."
Dame Seraphine shook her head slowly, her eyes shining, and said nothing yet. Whatever she was thinking, she was keeping it with her.
Botswana broke the quiet with a laugh of open incredulity. The scarred titan crossed the deck of the leaf toward him, and the permanent grim patience that hung on him faded.
"Brother," he said, "I had no idea you were carrying that around. An Echo of the Tongue."He shook his great head.

"An Echo does not bloom on a first grasp. It does not bloom on a thousandth grasp. It comes from a being who has spoken a letter of THE Primordial Tongue so many times, across so many ages, that their understanding of it grows a body and stands behind them. So how many years, exactly? How long have you been speaking, paired with whatever strange thing you are that you won’t tell us about, to manage that on your first attempt?"
How many years.
Noah’s eyes shone, and he kept the truth where it belonged. It had been a bit over a day?
A day, against the ages Botswana was imagining!
"Long enough," he said, and shook his head.

"Bahaha. Fine, fine, keep your secrets! Come. You scared poor William half to death back there, the man hasn’t sweated in an age. So settle the wager for the lot of us. Whose explanation of Destruere did the most for you...?"
The titan was friendly beneath all the violence he carried.

Noah traded words with the Swords of Existence, answered their questions, asked a few of his own, and somewhere in the middle of it he called Seo-yeon over. She came at once and jumped up onto his shoulder, settling there with her legs swinging, watching the strange powerful beings her Mister Noah had fallen in with as she took in everything.
Dame Seraphine kept her eyes on him through all of it, turning something over behind that shining composure, before she finally looked away and gazed out into the Gaps.
The Source Leaf-Vessel answered her attention, shooting forward ever faster, carrying the whole party deeper toward THE Arkethys Observable Existence.

It was a strange thing for Noah. He spent the bulk of his existence as a tyrant and a planner, a being who moved a dozen bodies across a dozen fronts and trusted almost no one with the seams between them.
The simple act of standing on a leaf cut from an impossible tree, bantering with a party of Swords of Existence who treated him as one of their own, was a change of pace he had not expected to enjoy.
And even as he stood there listening at something Botswana said, part of him turned away, toward another of his bodies, far from the leaf and the Gaps and the easy company.
In THE Infiniverse.

One body stood in THE Undefined Gaps with the weight of two Observable Existences crushing down on it, skin splitting and bones fracturing in an endless rhythm before the radiant flames of Persevere and Exelissomai surged up from his heart and made each ruined thing grander than it had been a breath before.
That body suffered. It was supposed to suffer!
This body was petting a dog.
Skoll leaned his whole massive frame into Noah’s hand, tail sweeping the empty space behind him with tremendous and uncomplicated joy, and Noah obliged the goodest boy ever.
They stood together in a realm that belonged to THE Prime Cause of Harvest, deep within THE Infiniverse.

The herbs grew straight out of space here. Crimson and gold Infinite Sacred Herbs rose from nothing, their roots reaching down not into soil but into the invisible strings and standing waves of the surrounding void, threading themselves into the Prime Cause of Harvest that saturated the region and drinking from it the way roots elsewhere drank water.

They blazed faintly, the crimson and the gold of them burning against the dark, and they stretched across dozens of plots that ran on and on without any horizon to stop them, an entire farm of cultivated power hanging suspended in the body of an Observable Existence.

Ruination stood beside him as her illusory self, a churning weave of Infinity lines. THE Infiniverse stood at his other side in her bejeweled multicolored dress, her form now threaded faintly with obsidian where the Primordial Source had taken root in her since she had drawn it into herself.

This body lived here, more or less. It was the one that stayed and talked, the one that sat with the two beings closest to the heart of everything he was building and worked through the ever-shifting weavings of existence around them, where to move, what to grow, how to plan. And right now, the plan on Noah’s mind was Arkethys.

"This supposedly anomalous Observable Existence,"he said, looking out across the endless plots, "with Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms killing each other over it for a million years, over a resource that produces Fourth Scale entities, elevates the rarity of an Intent, and can even help promote beings toward the Fifth Scale. It has started me thinking about all the different kinds of Observable Existences out there. The ones built for war, the ones built for knowledge, and now one that, by some accident of its malformed birth, grows the single best progression material either side has ever found."He turned to the two of them.
"And it made me ask a question. What prevents us from steering your evolution toward something similar to Arkethys?"
HUUM!
