She drank it, drew it through herself the way the void drew light, and gave back nothing at all.
His entire attack vanished into her and was gone, and the chamber of existence held still around the absence of it!
WAP!
Then the moment broke, and everything came loose at once.
The Leaf-Vessel steadied beneath their feet.
The Undefined Gaps resumed their black streaming past the obsidian-gold edges of the leaf.
The row of mirror-existences behind Noah thinned and faded back into the dark they had come from.
His eyes shone.
|You have glimpsed the power of a Mesozoic Scale being, briefly.
The mechanism appeared to draw your attack into her existence and dissolve it entirely rather than block or deflect it.
No true details could be discerned.
The gap between your perception and her actual capability remains too large to read.|
He read it and let it settle, and what stayed with him was not the failure to discern her power.
It was the casual completeness of how she had handled his!
He had put a great deal into that swing.
She had absorbed it the way a person absorbs a thrown crumb, without breaking stride, without changing expression, and then she had wiped the slate clean and let the vessel sail on.
That was the gap between the Fourth Scale and the Fifth, drawn for him in a single unhurried gesture!
He looked over and found sweat standing on Sir William’s forehead.
Noah gave a light cough.
"Apologies," he said."I was in a bit of a trance.
I may have taken the demonstration somewhat further than the demonstration required."
Dame Seraphine shook her head slowly, her eyes shining, and said nothing yet.
Whatever she was thinking, she was keeping it with her.
Botswana broke the quiet with a laugh of open incredulity.
The scarred titan crossed the deck of the leaf toward him, and the permanent grim patience that hung on him faded.
"Brother," he said, "I had no idea you were carrying that around.
An Echo of the Tongue."He shook his great head.
"An Echo does not bloom on a first grasp.
It does not bloom on a thousandth grasp.
It comes from a being who has spoken a letter of THE Primordial Tongue so many times, across so many ages, that their understanding of it grows a body and stands behind them.
So how many years, exactly?
How long have you been speaking, paired with whatever strange thing you are that you won’t tell us about, to manage that on your first attempt?"
How many years.
Noah’s eyes shone, and he kept the truth where it belonged.
It had been a bit over a day?
A day, against the ages Botswana was imagining!
"Long enough," he said, and shook his head.
"Bahaha.
Fine, fine, keep your secrets!
Come.
You scared poor William half to death back there, the man hasn’t sweated in an age.
So settle the wager for the lot of us.
Whose explanation of Destruere did the most for you...?"
The titan was friendly beneath all the violence he carried.
Noah traded words with the Swords of Existence, answered their questions, asked a few of his own, and somewhere in the middle of it he called Seo-yeon over.
She came at once and jumped up onto his shoulder, settling there with her legs swinging, watching the strange powerful beings her Mister Noah had fallen in with as she took in everything.
Dame Seraphine kept her eyes on him through all of it, turning something over behind that shining composure, before she finally looked away and gazed out into the Gaps.
The Source Leaf-Vessel answered her attention, shooting forward ever faster, carrying the whole party deeper toward THE Arkethys Observable Existence.
It was a strange thing for Noah.
He spent the bulk of his existence as a tyrant and a planner, a being who moved a dozen bodies across a dozen fronts and trusted almost no one with the seams between them.
The simple act of standing on a leaf cut from an impossible tree, bantering with a party of Swords of Existence who treated him as one of their own, was a change of pace he had not expected to enjoy.
And even as he stood there listening at something Botswana said, part of him turned away, toward another of his bodies, far from the leaf and the Gaps and the easy company.
In THE Infiniverse.

One body stood in THE Undefined Gaps with the weight of two Observable Existences crushing down on it, skin splitting and bones fracturing in an endless rhythm before the radiant flames of Persevere and Exelissomai surged up from his heart and made each ruined thing grander than it had been a breath before.
That body suffered.
It was supposed to suffer!
This body was petting a dog.
Skoll leaned his whole massive frame into Noah’s hand, tail sweeping the empty space behind him with tremendous and uncomplicated joy, and Noah obliged the goodest boy ever.
They stood together in a realm that belonged to THE Prime Cause of Harvest, deep within THE Infiniverse.
The herbs grew straight out of space here.

Crimson and gold Infinite Sacred Herbs rose from nothing, their roots reaching down not into soil but into the invisible strings and standing waves of the surrounding void, threading themselves into the Prime Cause of Harvest that saturated the region and drinking from it the way roots elsewhere drank water.

They blazed faintly, the crimson and the gold of them burning against the dark, and they stretched across dozens of plots that ran on and on without any horizon to stop them, an entire farm of cultivated power hanging suspended in the body of an Observable Existence.
Ruination stood beside him as her illusory self, a churning weave of Infinity lines.

THE Infiniverse stood at his other side in her bejeweled multicolored dress, her form now threaded faintly with obsidian where the Primordial Source had taken root in her since she had drawn it into herself.
This body lived here, more or less.

It was the one that stayed and talked, the one that sat with the two beings closest to the heart of everything he was building and worked through the ever-shifting weavings of existence around them, where to move, what to grow, how to plan.
And right now, the plan on Noah’s mind was Arkethys.

"This supposedly anomalous Observable Existence,"he said, looking out across the endless plots, "with Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms killing each other over it for a million years, over a resource that produces Fourth Scale entities, elevates the rarity of an Intent, and can even help promote beings toward the Fifth Scale.
It has started me thinking about all the different kinds of Observable Existences out there.

The ones built for war, the ones built for knowledge, and now one that, by some accident of its malformed birth, grows the single best progression material either side has ever found."He turned to the two of them.
"And it made me ask a question.
What prevents us from steering your evolution toward something similar to Arkethys?"
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5356: Guided Evolution! II
paragraphs: The words came out casual and tyrannical in the same breath, the way most of his best ideas did, and Ruination and THE Infiniverse looked at each other with shining eyes before THE Infiniverse answered him.

"The large concentrations of Pure Primordial Essence, and now the Primordial Source you have given me, all of it is pulling and tugging at the boundless Infinity that runs through THE Infinite Cause,"she said.

"Paired with Persevere and Exelissomai echoing through me every single second, refining me without pause, I have a great deal of room in what I choose to become. I can steer my growth. I can finish my evolution with a clear aim in mind, a resource close to the one they killed each other for in Arkethys. Perhaps, in time, one even grander."She paused, and there was something almost wry in it.

"There is no template for us, Master. We are not walking anyone’s road. We could become anything we are able to envision, so long as it sits within the bounds of the authority we hold. So the envisioning is the whole of the work."
She looked out at the endless plots of Infinite Sacred Herbs, and for a moment she seemed to be seeing past them, to what the fields could become.
"I will begin now," she said. "Giving my evolution a direction should let me finish it faster than blooming aimlessly would..."
As she spoke, the realm began to tremble.

THE Infiniverse rose. Multicolored Infinity glimmered off her in slow waves, braided through with the obsidian brilliance of the Primordial Source, the two great authorities turning together through her manifestation as she bent the whole of her boundless potential toward a single deliberate aim!

An entire Observable Existence, guiding the grandest stage of its own becoming, steering itself toward something immaculate, a domain that might one day grow the kind of resource that civilizations had slaughtered each other over for a million years!
The rivers came to her then.

Through the realm flowed Infinity and Observable Force and Unobservable Force in slow deep currents, and here and there, scattered through the crimson and gold light like dark stars fallen into water, drifted slivers of the Primordial Source.

All of it passed through the manifestation of THE Infiniverse where she stood at the center of the field, gathering the streams into herself, drawing the raw material of the work into one place. She turned her head and nodded to her sister.
Ruination nodded back, and her churning Infinity lines bent toward the open space between them and Noah.
An object began to rise there.
It was illusory still, a proposal rather than a thing, a model assembled from the gathered authorities so that Noah could see what they meant to grow before they grew it.

Rigid silver-white roots formed first, anchoring themselves straight into the spatial fabric of existence, gripping the void the way the Infinite Sacred Herbs did but thicker than they were, deeper, hungrier.

The plant put up no leaves. It raised a single thick stalk, plain and unadorned, with nothing decorative about it at all. And at the crown of that stalk, the fruit took shape, a heavy obsidian sphere, dense and dark and quietly enormous in the way it sat in the air, radiating a direct and unmediated presence that pressed on the surrounding region with none of the softening that most things kept between themselves and the world.
Noah watched the whole of it form inside THE Infiniverse’s manifestation, the proposed resource assembling itself in front of him piece by piece.
|Proposed resource, first design for review. Designation: THE Primordial Source-Blood.|

|Form: A rooted plant anchored into the spatial fabric of THE Infiniverse, drawing nutrients directly from the region’s Prime Cause of Harvest and the ambient Pure Primordial Essence. A single stalk, no leaves, bearing a single heavy obsidian fruit.|

|Core property: The fruit holds concentrated Pure Primordial Essence within it. Consuming the refined fruit fortifies the foundation and the Source of any lifeform, delivering the full boons of Pure Primordial Essence straight into the consumer’s existence.|
|Expanded properties under the proposed design:|

|The fruit adapts its delivery to whoever eats it. A weak lifeform receives a measured, survivable influx that strengthens their foundation without tearing them apart. A strong lifeform receives a volume scaled to whatever they can hold, with no ceiling imposed by the fruit itself.|
|Consumption quickens the consumer’s rate of progression across the Scales of Existence, easing the forming of their foundation and smoothing the hard thresholds between stages.|

|The Pure Primordial Essence it delivers carries no alignment of its own, so it integrates cleanly with any path, any Cause, any Ego, or any Source the consumer already holds, refining what is there rather than warring with it.|
|The fruit regrows on the stalk after harvest, drawing fresh Pure Primordial Essence from the region. In a mature field, THE Primordial Source-Blood becomes a renewable and perpetual supply.|
|This is the first proposed material. Refinements and alternatives can follow if it does not satisfy.|
Noah’s eyes lit as he read.

He turned the thing over in his mind, hunting for the flaw, the hidden cost, anything! He found none worth raising. A renewable fruit that fed Pure Primordial Essence into anyone who ate it, scaled itself to what each consumer could survive, aligned to nothing so it conflicted with nothing.
It was precisely the kind of thing that turned a sheltered Civilization hiding in the dark into a civilization of Existences to be feared!
He had, for once, no complaints at all.
"Let’s go with this one first," he said.
|Understood.|
HUUM!

The realm trembled harder. The region steeped in THE Prime Cause of Harvest gathered its full authority, and the rivers of Infinity and Primordial Source bent inward, converging on the single proposed stalk, the streams pouring toward one point in the dark.
THE Infiniverse turned the weight of her evolving power toward bringing the first specimen into being, drawing the model out of proposal and into truth.
This was the start of it. The first emergence of a material built for one purpose and one purpose only, to make the long murderous climb across the Scales of Existence feel like child’s play!
It was only the first. There had to be much more for Noah himself to be satisfied as his Tyranny...was insatiable!

chapters.title: Chapter 5357: It Reigns Supreme! I
paragraphs: Some will tell you THE Primordial Source is the first thing.The foundation. The bedrock everything else was poured upon, and Infinity merely a guest who arrived late and overstayed his welcome.

They tell you this because they are Source Lifeforms and the fable flatters them, and a lie told often enough by the powerful becomes a truth the weak recite without ever once checking it. So check it.Ask one question.

THE Primordial Source is finite. It comes in units. It can be mined, hoarded, exhausted, spent down to nothing. What kind of foundation runs dry? Infinity does not run dry. Infinity is the single authority in all of existence that cannot be depleted, cannot be cornered, cannot be told there is no more left in the cup.

THE Primordial Source is a vault, and every vault, however vast, has a floor you reach eventually. Infinity is the open sky, and the sky has no floor at all. They worship the vault because they were born clutching its key, and they call us the lesser ones for reaching toward the sky instead. Let them.The sky was never theirs to rank.
<Recovered Akashic Record, attributed to an unnamed Infinite Lifeform>
<Arkethys Observable Existence>
The region felt older and grander than the idea of old and grand!

It was a place of space and metal and crystal, and across spans no chronicle had survived to record, the three had grown so thoroughly into one another that you could no longer say where stone ended and void began.

Crystalline formations rose out of the dark in great fractured columns, shining obsidian blue and the deep starless black of true noir, their faces catching a light that fell from no sun anywhere, light that lived inside the stone itself, born of the bound authorities suspended in its lattice.

Veins of metal ran through the crystal in ancient bands, layer on layer like strata laid down across unthinkable time, and where those veins broke the surface they glowed faintly with the trapped Infinity and Primordial Source that made Arkethys the thing both sides had died for.
There was no ground here, not in any honest sense. No Folds, no Wheels of Existence, no Wandering Territories.

The whole region drifted, its crystalline landmasses hanging in a void that pressed on everything within it with a quiet lethal weight, the kind that ended Third Scale beings through nothing more than proximity, and all of it turned in slow and ancient orbits around a single fixed point.
At a point in a small region of this Observable Existence stood a tree.

It rose from the largest of the drifting landmasses, trunk and branches grown from the same obsidian-blue crystal as the region around it, and it was vast enough that the thousands of figures floating in attendance around it registered as little more than motes of light against its bulk.

The figures were beautiful in a sharp and cold way, tall and fine-boned, their ears tapering to points, and they carried themselves with the arrogance of a people who had decided a very long time ago that they were superior.

They wore blue glowing armor that burned with Infinity and Existential Radiation, and across every span of their skin ran runic tattoos of blue and gold, pulsing in slow unison, each line of them carrying Infinity threaded together with an Ego. Superbius in some. Humilitas in others. Invidia, Gula, Patientia, a whole spectrum of cultivated emotion written directly into living flesh.
These were Infinite Lifeforms. Many stood at the Fourth Scale!
A few carried the lesser weight of the Third. And every last one of them floated around the crystalline tree with the watchful stillness of guardians set to protect something at its heart.
Past them, deeper in, the tree held an innermost chamber.
And in that chamber waited nine beings, every one of them at the Fifth Scale of Existence. THE Mesozoic Scale!
Nine, gathered together in a single place, a concentration of power so heavy that no ordinary domain could have held it without buckling beneath the load.

That was the Treaty’s work. The agreement that kept Arkethys from finishing the old war demanded a balance of strength, and balance at the highest tier meant each side stationed Mesozoic Scale beings within the domain, watching the Seam and watching each other, their mere presence the heaviest stone on the scale that held the peace level.
Nine Fifth Scale Infinite Lifeforms here.

Among the nine stood a man with blue-gold hair and two horns rising from his brow, wrapped in a blue robe through which turned a slow crown of Infinity and Avaritia, the Ego of greed revolving above his head like a halo that had curdled.

He watched the other eight. They were gathered close around something at the chamber’s center, their gazes apprehensive, their hands held out toward a spinning singularity into which they were pouring their Akashic Civilizational Intents and a great deal more besides.
The singularity felt wrong.
There was no clean way to say it. It spun, and it pulled, and the pull reached past the body into something underneath the body, and the wrongness of it was unique.

It was the wrongness of a thing that ought not to be allowed to exist at all, a vile note held low beneath the hum of the chamber, the kind of sound that set every instinct a being owned on edge at once.
One of those nearest the singularity turned to the horned man, and hesitation sat plain in her eyes.

"Borys," she said. "Should we truly proceed with this? We are reaching a point we cannot come back from. The Source Lifeforms have felt the instabilities rising. They have begun to move. Once we do this thing, we cannot stop it. We will not be able to stop it. It will be open war, all of it, everywhere, at once."
HUUM!
Borys looked on calmly.

"War," he said, and turned the word over as though tasting it. "You say it as though it would be some sort of departure. As though we have been doing anything else this whole time."He folded his hands in front of him.
HUUM!

"We have always been at war. From the very beginning, Infinite Lifeforms and Source Lifeforms have been at war with one another, and there have been so many of these wars, so very many, that some of our own people have honestly lost the count. They remember the stretches of peace and they forget the wars between them, which is a charming sort of optimism and an absolutely fatal sort of stupidity. The last war we lost was against Vakochev. That is the most recent one. It is not the only one. And the true Infinite Lifeforms, the ones who actually remember, we do not forget our hatred. We carry it. We have carried it the entire time, tucked underneath our existence..."
He stepped closer to the singularity, and the crown of greed turned faster above him.

"And who...could possibly have guessed,"he went on, something like delight warming his voice, "that Arkethys, this lethal little rock we have all been so politely sharing for a million years, was hiding something like this inside it. Something the Source Lifeforms, with all their precious Primordial Source and all their breathtaking superiority, cannot so much as imagine is here. They have not the faintest idea what we found waiting here..."

His eyes caught the light of the spinning thing. "This will be a glorious spark. We have to continue. Do you understand me? We do not have the luxury of stopping now, because a thing like this does not arrive twice, and a people who flinch away from the single chance they are ever given have earned every year of the supremacy they suffer under. We can only continue. So we will."
HUUM!

Something the Source Lifeforms, with all their precious Primordial Source and all their breathtaking superiority, cannot so much as imagine is here.
They have not the faintest idea what we found waiting here..."
His eyes caught the light of the spinning thing.
"This will be a glorious spark.
We have to continue.
Do you understand me?

We do not have the luxury of stopping now, because a thing like this does not arrive twice, and a people who flinch away from the single chance they are ever given have earned every year of the supremacy they suffer under.
We can only continue.
So we will."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5358: It Reigns Supreme! II
paragraphs: The instant the words left his mouth, his own Akashic Civilizational Intent erupted out of him and flooded into the singularity.
It spun faster. Faster still, drinking down the Intent, winding tighter and tighter, and then, in the very next breath.
BOOM! CRACK!

Crystalline metallic cracks tore outward in every direction at once, and space itself split, permanently, the fracture racing through the chamber and up through the great tree and out across the drifting region beyond it, all of it accompanied by a sound like the world’s own bones breaking clean through. And something began to leak from the singularity. Something that had been waiting on the other side of it!
A decrepit gray-blue finger pushed out of the spinning point.

It paused there a moment, turning, taking in the chamber, the nine Fifth Scale beings, the crystalline tree, the spreading fracture in the fabric of the world, the way a thing wakes and looks around a room it has just entered!

And then it shot toward Borys at a speed that even Fifth Scale existences could not track, crossing the whole chamber before any of them had finished registering that it had begun to move, and it drove into his chest and sank in to the knuckle and beyond!
BOOM!
Borys felt the impact only after it had already happened.

And what crossed his face was a glorious, shining excitement. His existence began to buzz, low and rising, the crown of Infinity and Avaritia spinning faster and faster above his horns, and he laughed, soft and delighted and entirely without fear, as his whole being filled with an air of oppression so heavy that the other eight Mesozoic Scale beings drew back from him, away from whatever it was he was turning into!
His hand rose and touched his own face, fingertips against his cheek, as if to confirm he was still there underneath the buzzing.

"The supremacy of the Source Lifeforms must come to an end," he said, very softly."It must. We are weak. I will be the first one in this chamber to say it plainly, because the ones who cannot bring themselves to say it are exactly the ones who stay weak forever. We are not the great deciders of wars and struggles. We do not sit at the top of existence handing down our judgments to the rest. But everything has to start somewhere. Even the weak can begin a change, if only they are willing to become something the strong never thought to account for."
His buzzing existence pressed outward through the broken chamber.

"So from this moment forward, we wage war against the supremacy of the Source Lifeforms. We have to. We have. For who are they, who has any of them ever been, to look at Infinity and rank it beneath THE Primordial Source?"
His eyes burned in the fractured dark.
"Infinity reigns supreme. It reigns supreme. It has to. It has to."
HUUM!
The Source Leaf-Vessel broke out of THE Undefined Gaps, and Arkethys opened around them like something that had been waiting a very long time to be looked at.

The first thing was the light. It came from nowhere and everywhere, born inside the stone itself rather than falling from any sun, an obsidian blue glow that lived in the crystal and the metal and pulsed faintly with the bound authorities suspended in their lattice. The region drifted in pieces, vast crystalline landmasses turning in slow ancient orbits through a void that pressed down on everything within it, and across those landmasses the banded veins of metal caught the glow and threw it back in colors that had no names, deep noir shot through with blue, the whole place shining like the inside of something that should not have been opened!
Noah took it in with the calm of a being who had seen a great many domains and still found this one worth a moment of his attention.
|Arrival confirmed: THE Arkethys Observable Existence.|

|Environmental composition: A void domain saturated with bound, unstable Infinity and Primordial Source, the signature of Eridarch Ore distributed throughout the crystalline strata. The ambient pressure of these two authorities, held in their unnatural lattice, exerts continuous environmental harm on any existence present. Third Scale beings perish from prolonged exposure alone. The domain grows more unstable the more it is mined, and current readings indicate the instability is rising. Disturbance of Ore deposits risks cascade detonation. Treat the air itself as a hazard.|
The warning was accurate. Noah could feel it, the slow grinding pressure that wanted into his foundations, the bound Infinity and Primordial Source pressing on him from every direction at once!
It landed on him like rain on a roof.

He stood on the deck of the leaf with Seo-yeon on his shoulder, and the two of them simply withstood the environment of Arkethys without doing anything about it at all. He did not raise a defense. He did not channel his Aura. He did not need to!
Hah!

THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian sat over his existence as a permanent expression, and the Pure Primordial Source budding within him drank the ambient pressure as though it were a courtesy rather than a threat.

Beside his ear, Seo-yeon watched the drifting crystal with bright curious eyes, equally untroubled, her dual nature as both Infinite and Source Lifeform making the lethal air of the place feel to her like weather she happened to find pretty.
She continued to be a terrifying existence!

The Swords noticed. Botswana glanced at the pair of them, at the new Sword and the small girl standing comfortably in an atmosphere that demanded active defense from everyone else aboard, and said nothing, though his grim mouth twitched at one corner.

Dame Seraphine guided the Leaf-Vessel inward, toward a structure rising out of the largest cluster of drifting landmasses, and that structure resolved as they neared it into a citadel built around mines.

It was a citadel of crystalline excavation, towers and halls and great open shafts grown and carved from the same obsidian-blue crystal as everything else, the whole of it organized around the veins of Eridarch Ore that ran beneath and through it.

Scaffolding of pale metal threaded the shafts. Refineries glowed at the citadel’s heart, slow and careful, the controlled extraction that the Treaty of Arkethys demanded. And moving through all of it, thousands of them, were Source Lifeforms.
Noah read the weight of them as the leaf descended. Many at the Fourth Scale, their Existential Radiation pressing in dense controlled coils.
And not a few at the Fifth, THE Mesozoic Scale, moving among the lesser ones with the unhurried gravity of beings the rest of the citadel organized itself around.
The leaf settled, and a small group came to meet them.

Three Fifth Scale existences stood at the front of the welcome, beings of obsidian gravity whose presence pressed even against the ambient hostility of Arkethys and made the air around them feel, by contrast, almost still.
They inclined their heads to Dame Seraphine with the respect of equals greeting an equal, the specific courtesy of powerful beings who did not extend such courtesy lightly.
"Seraphine," the foremost of them said, a tall figure whose Existential Radiation ran the color of deep water. "Haha, you came yourself. We are glad its you!"

chapters.title: Chapter 5359: Instability I
paragraphs: Then the being’s gaze moved past her, to Noah, and to the small girl on his shoulder, and openly considered the both of them with interest.

"Though I confess, when we sent word to THE Hallowed Demesne asking for help with what is happening here, we did not imagine the answer would arrive in the form of a new Sword. I literally had to do a double take when you sent that message that you were escorting the potential solution over..."The gaze lingered, assessing.
"And a child. You will forgive our curiosity. Arkethys is not where one brings the newly sworn"
"You will forgive mine in turn if I keep the reasoning to myself for now,Andro" Dame Seraphine said evenly.
"The Order came from above. From THE Domicile. I assume that answers more than my explanation would."
That shifted the attention in the three Fifth Scale beings!
The foremost one’s eyes sharpened, and the courtesy in his bearing deepened into something closer to gravity.
"From THE Domicile..."
He gestured around at the citadel and the drifting region beyond it.

"You understand why. THE Domicile of THE Queen Regnant counts Arkethys among the important holdings of the forces under Her Majesty. Through this place, through the Ore in its strata, we produce Fourth Scale Source Lifeforms in numbers, and we elevate beings toward the Fifth who would otherwise never reach it. Haha, Arkethys is a forge! A glorious forge! It makes the strong that the rest of Her Majesty’s purposes require. So when the forge begins to crack, the matter rises very quickly to the top."

He turned, the obsidian glow sliding across his features. "Hmm, which is why I will not waste your time with hospitality you did not come for. Why don’t we take you to one of the regions showing the greatest instability? You can see for yourselves what we are dealing with."
Dame Seraphine nodded once. "Lead on, big guy."

The three Fifth Scale beings turned and moved deeper into the citadel, and the party followed, out of the relative shelter of the structure’s heart and back toward the open shafts where the drifting crystal hung in the lethal blue dark.
Noah observed and analyzed everything very closely!

The environment pressed in again the moment they left the citadel’s core, the bound Infinity and Primordial Source grinding at every existence that passed through it, and the Swords held their defenses steady as they walked.
Richard kept up a low running commentary to no one in particular, his bright eyes cataloguing the strata they passed.
Botswana walked in grim silence, one hand never far from where his Armament rested. Lianna gave nothing away, her composed gaze moving across the citadel’s workers and the drifting landmasses.

Noah walked through it all with Seo-yeon riding easy on his shoulder, the killing air of Arkethys landing on the two of them like nothing at all, and let his perception spread out across the region ahead.
They crossed gigaparsecs worth of distance before ultimately...they arrived where they needed to be!
The region showing the most instability was a massive, endless stretching Mine!
The entrance to the mine waited for them like the open mouth of something that ate.
It was a cluster vast enough to measure in light years, a wound carved into a drifting crystalline continent.

Jagged crystal teeth of obsidian blue framed the opening, the throat of it descending into a dark that the ambient glow of Arkethys did not reach, and the whole thing sat there with the patient hunger of a beast that had already eaten a great many things and was prepared to eat a great many more.
Only a scattering of Source Lifeforms remained near it, a handful of Fourth Scale beings and two of the Fifth, and even they kept a careful distance from the mouth of the Mine!
Noah understood why the moment he turned his attention to the region itself.
It was...pulsing.

The whole cluster, the mine and the crystal around it and the drifting dark beyond, beat in a slow steady rhythm, in and out, like a heart that had no business being where it was. And the Pulse was not idle!

He could feel it reaching into the bound authorities of the place and pulling at them, working at the Infinity and the Primordial Source in the strata, loosening something that had been holding them in their unnatural balance. It was the source of the instability!

|Analysis: An Unstable Pulse of unknown origin is propagating through this region of Arkethys. The Pulse acts directly upon the foundational makeup of lifeforms and authorities present, destabilizing both Infinity and THE Primordial Source. Its mechanism is not depletion or damage in the ordinary sense. It changes the nature of each authority into something else, a foreign and unstable nature that belongs to neither.|

|Effect on lifeforms: Existences exposed to the Pulse for long enough undergo a breakdown in their own Source makeup. The authorities that compose them are converted toward this foreign nature, and as the conversion spreads, the identity of the existence is altered and then erased, leaving something unrecognizable and unstable in its place. Weaker existences are altered fastest. The deeper into the Pulse one travels, the faster the breakdown.|
|Assessment: This is not a natural instability. Something is doing this. Cause unconfirmed.|
Noah’s existence buzzed!

This was not the grinding environmental pressure of Arkethys, the simple weight that tried to wear an existence down. This was subtler and worse. The Pulse reached past his power and toward the thing underneath his power, toward what he was, and it tried to convert that into something foreign, something that was no longer him!
Even Seo-yeon frowned at it, her bright untroubled face creasing as she felt the Pulse working at the deep structure she saw so clearly in everything, including herself.
And Noah, turning his attention inward, found what was defending him.
It was not THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian, not primarily, though the Aura helped.
It was Osmontian Absolute Infinity.His Infinity, with his identity forged into its foundation rather than dissolved away from it, was the precise thing the Pulse could not get a grip on!

The Pulse worked by converting nature and erasing identity, and Noah had spent his everything making his identity the unbreakable core of his Infinity, putting himself first and the boundlessness second, refusing the version of Absolute Infinity that ate the self. Here, in a place that murdered beings by eating the self, that choice was the wall that kept him whole!

Seo-yeon was less protected. Her dual nature was extraordinary, but she was young, and the Pulse worked fastest on the young as her identity was not fully fleshed out. So he extended THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian over her, wrapping the obsidian gold of it around her small frame, and her identity steadied inside the shelter of his own.
She smiled at once, the frown gone, and hugged his head.
"Thank you!"she murmured against his hair, and went back to watching the terrible beautiful mine with her curiosity fully restored!

chapters.title: Chapter 5360: Instability II
paragraphs: The Fifth Scale being who had been speaking with Dame Seraphine the whole way, the tall figure named Andro, gestured toward the gaping entrance.

"This is THE Maw,"he said,"It was our richest mine. We pulled the greatest share of our Eridarch Ore from THE Maw for longer than most of the workers here have existed. It produced more strength for Her Majesty’s forces than any other shaft in Arkethys."
His Existential Radiation, the color of deep water, dimmed slightly as he spoke.

"And then it began to change. The deeper one goes now, the more unstable existence becomes. The Pulse you can feel is faint here at the mouth. It worsens with depth. Past a certain point inward, both Infinity and the Primordial Source come apart entirely, unraveled into that foreign nature, and only Fifth Scale beings can hold their own identities together against it. Below that, we do not know, because we stopped sending anyone below it. We had to stop mining THE Maw. Our richest vein, and we abandoned it, because every attempt to work it now ends with the workers ceasing to be themselves."
Dame Seraphine frowned and looked around the drifting region, her gaze moving across the crystal and the dark.
"The Infinite Lifeforms,"she said. "Their movements. Have they had anything to do with this? An instability that conveniently weakens the Source side of a domain..."

"We thought the same," Andro said. "We watched closely. But they have been quiet, for the most part. Quieter than usual, if anything. And none of them have crossed into our borders. Whatever this is, it rose up out of our own ground."
Dame Seraphine stood with that for a moment, thinking, her composed features giving little away. Then she turned to Noah.
"You feel it as well as I do," she said."Are you comfortable going in to take a look?"
Noah rolled his neck and stretched, easy and unbothered, Seo-yeon swaying gently on his shoulder.
"Let’s go," he said.
They entered THE Maw, joined only by Andro, the other Source Lifeforms remaining behind at the mouth, and the dark closed over them as they descended.

|Environment: Interior of THE Maw. Ambient hostility increasing with depth. Environmental pressures and Pulse intensity rising. Raging existential winds present, carrying the foreign converted nature; capable of cutting into the existence of any being whose Akashic Civilizational Intent is of insufficient rarity to ward it. Continue with caution.|
Inside, the mine was a vast hollow throat of obsidian blue crystal, the carved walls still bearing the marks of long mining, scaffolding of pale metal hanging abandoned in the deeper reaches.

And the winds came almost at once, raging existential gusts that carried the converted foreign nature on them, sweeping up through the shaft, the kind of wind that would have flayed the existence off any being whose Intent was too weak to turn it aside. It tried to cut into all of them!
WUU! WUU! WUU!

Noah withstood it without effort and kept the Aura wrapped firm around Seo-yeon, the two of them passing through the flaying wind untouched. The other consideration was the Swords as they were strong enough to withstand all this, and Andro held his own with the unbothered steadiness of a Fifth Scale being on familiar ground!
They delved deeper.

The Pulse strengthened with every length of descent, the beating of it growing heavier, the foreign nature pressing harder against every existence in the shaft. And then, as they passed through a turning in the great crystal throat, his own existence pulled at him.
Not toward danger. Towards... want! Towards Loot! His senses were tingling!

His foundations, steeped now in Infinity and THE Primordial Source, recognized something ahead and leaned toward it. He shifted the group’s direction, turning them away from the path Andro had been following and toward the pull, and in doing so he steered them into a vibrant storm that would have clouded one’s vision!
Beyond the storm, set into the crystal wall, a cluster of Eridarch Ore shone.

It was the banded crystalline metal he had been told about and had not yet seen, dark and layered and luminous, each band holding its thread of Infinity beside its thread of Primordial Source, the two authorities suspended together in defiance of every law that should have annihilated them. It glowed in the dark of THE Maw with a light that was almost gentle, which felt like a lie given everything he knew it was worth and everything it had cost.
Andro looked at the cluster, and then at Noah, with new attention.
"Someone with a nose like yours should have been brought here a great deal sooner,"he said. He drifted closer to the Ore, careful not to touch it.

"Eridarch Ore can be drawn out using either Infinity or the Primordial Source. You channel the authority into the lattice, match it to the thread of its own kind, and coax the band free. It takes vast reserves to do it, because the Ore does not give itself up easily. The half of it that responds to you is terrifying enough on its own. But the other half, the opposite authority, resists. And if you mine it wrong, if you let the two threads come out of balance, the Infinity and the Primordial Source within the Ore clash...and they explode."His voice flattened.
"An explosion from a single improperly mined cluster can wipe out an Einherjar Source. Or a weak Fourth Scale equivalent. Clean off the board, identity and all."
He gestured at the shaft around them, at the abandoned scaffolding and the raging wind.

"And recently, with the Pulse worsening, the balance has become impossible to hold. Every attempt to mine, no matter how careful, ends in collapse. In death. That is the other reason we stopped working THE Maw. It was that the Ore itself stopped letting us take it without killing us for the trouble."
Noah looked at the cluster of Eridarch Ore, at the gentle deadly glow of it in the dark, and made a decision.
"Wait here," he told Seo-yeon, and lifted her gently from his shoulder, setting her in place behind him."I want to look at something."
He floated ahead, toward the shining cluster, alone.

And Dame Seraphine floated up beside him as he went, not crowding him, but close, her Mesozoic Scale presence settling at his flank with the quiet readiness of a being prepared to put herself between him and whatever happened next, should the Ore or the Pulse or the Maw itself decide to be problematic!
Noah reached the cluster of Eridarch Ore and did not channel Infinity into it, and he did not channel THE Primordial Source into it, because both of those were the methods that got beings killed.
He used THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian instead.

The Aura was the one expression he had that held everything at once, Infinity and Primordial Source and the nine Prime Causes and the Observable and Unobservable Force, all of it integrated and amplified through the wild anomalous nature of THE Source Barbarian.

So rather than matching one thread of the Ore and fighting the other, he reached out with the whole of it, the obsidian gold settling over the shining cluster, and met both threads at once. The Infinity in the lattice found Infinity in his Aura. THE Primordial Source in the lattice found Primordial Source in his Aura.

Neither thread was left to resist while the other was coaxed, because he was offering both of them a home in the same motion, and the Ore, which had killed careful Source Lifeforms for refusing to come out in balance, came out in perfect balance because balance was the only thing Noah wanted!
HUUM!

The band of Eridarch Ore lifted free of the crystal wall, intact, unexploded, drifting into the obsidian gold of his Aura without so much as a flicker of the clash that had been wiping out Source Lifeforms across the recent months!

|Properties: A crystalline metal in which pure stable Infinity and Primordial Source are bound together in a single lattice.Among the most effective progression materials for Third, Fourth, and Fifth Scale beings in existence.Refining with Eridarch Ore allows a lifeform to smoothly form their Akashic Civilizational Intent and step into the Fourth Scale, and has shown the capacity to elevate an Intent toward a higher rarity, as well as to ease the path toward the Fifth Scale.|

|Your Aura of THE Source Barbarian is reacting to the Ore. THE Aura currently functions as a unified expression of all your capabilities but does not hold a formal Akashic Civilizational Intent designation, as you exist outside Vakochev’s Scales. The bound nature of Eridarch Ore is compatible with the Aura’s structure.Refining a sufficient quantity of Eridarch Ore into THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian may grant the Aura an official identity as an Akashic Civilizational Intent, formalizing what it already does into a recognized record imposed upon existence.|
Noah turned that over with genuine interest.

His Aura already behaved like an Intent. It had pressed on Fourth Scale beings and felt heavier than a third-rarity Intent when he unleashed it, and yet it carried no formal designation, because he was off the Scales entirely and the framework had no slot to put him in!

The Ore offered to give the Aura a name in the language existence actually spoke, to turn the thing he had built into a record that reality would formally acknowledge, the way it acknowledged the Intents of every Fourth and Fifth Scale being.
He put the band of Eridarch Ore away in his existence, and sent his directions inward to Ruination.
Analyze it. All of it. Determine whether something like this could be replicated, grown, produced deliberately in THE Infiniverse.
|Understood. Beginning full analysis.|
He was about to turn back to Dame Seraphine, to say something, when the Maw changed around them!
HUUM!
Deep below, far past the depths Andro had said the Source Lifeforms no longer went, something triggered.

The Pulse, which had been beating in its slow heavy rhythm the whole way down, lost the rhythm. It went chaotic, the steady beat breaking into something erratic and rising, and the foreign converted nature that rode on it surged up through the shaft with new violence!
The raging existential winds tore harder. The instability climbed, and every being in the depths felt it at once, the whole of THE Maw shuddering as whatever sat at its bottom stirred!
Noah focused on the instability, and the light of his Infinite Cause began to bloom around him.

He reached out with it, the way he had reached into Chernobyl, checking the integrity of the domain at the foundational level, examining THE First Cause of Arkethys and the Prime Causes built into it. He expected to find what he had found in Chernobyl!
Deterioration. Failing Causes guttering toward collapse, a domain coming apart at its foundation, the familiar shape of an Observable Existence beginning to die.
He found nothing of the kind!
Oh!

He found, to his genuine astonishment, that the Prime Causes of Arkethys were vibrant. Not deteriorating. Not guttering. Not failing in any direction he could read. They blazed with strength, every one of them, more vigorous than the Causes of a domain in this state had any right to be!

|Analysis of THE First Cause of Arkethys: The Prime Causes of this Observable Existence are not deteriorating. They are, by every standard measure, stronger than ever. However, their identity and standing have been altered by an unfathomable force. They exhibit qualities never before observed in their respective natures. The Prime Causes themselves have been influenced by an unstable weaving that is transforming what each one stands for, converting their fundamental meaning into something else.|

|The instability of Arkethys does not originate from failing Causes. It originates from Causes that are being changed. The domain is not dying. The domain is becoming something older, other than what it was, at the level of its foundational truths, and the lifeforms and authorities within it are being dragged along into that same foreign nature.|
Noah frowned, THE Infinite Cause light churning around him!

The foundational truths of the entire Observable Existence were being altered, converted, transformed into something they had not been, and everything else, the Pulse, the unraveling of Infinity and Primordial Source, the erasure of identities, was downstream of that!
Something had reached into the bedrock truths that Arkethys was built on and begun rewriting them!

The winds raged harder, the chaotic Pulse climbing, the foreign nature pressing in from every surface of THE Maw, and Dame Seraphine’s composed features tightened as she felt the depths stir toward something none of them could yet see.
"Pull back!"she said.

"This is THE Maw,"he said,"It was our richest mine.
We pulled the greatest share of our Eridarch Ore from THE Maw for longer than most of the workers here have existed.

His Existential Radiation, the color of deep water, dimmed slightly as he spoke.
"And then it began to change.
The deeper one goes now, the more unstable existence becomes.
The Pulse you can feel is faint here at the mouth.
It worsens with depth.

Past a certain point inward, both Infinity and the Primordial Source come apart entirely, unraveled into that foreign nature, and only Fifth Scale beings can hold their own identities together against it.
Below that, we do not know, because we stopped sending anyone below it.
We had to stop mining THE Maw.
Our richest vein, and we abandoned it, because every attempt to work it now ends with the workers ceasing to be themselves."
Dame Seraphine frowned and looked around the drifting region, her gaze moving across the crystal and the dark.
"The Infinite Lifeforms,"she said.
"Their movements.
Have they had anything to do with this?
An instability that conveniently weakens the Source side of a domain..."
"We thought the same," Andro said.
"We watched closely.
But they have been quiet, for the most part.
Quieter than usual, if anything.
And none of them have crossed into our borders.
Whatever this is, it rose up out of our own ground."
Dame Seraphine stood with that for a moment, thinking, her composed features giving little away.
Then she turned to Noah.
"You feel it as well as I do," she said."Are you comfortable going in to take a look?"
Noah rolled his neck and stretched, easy and unbothered, Seo-yeon swaying gently on his shoulder.
"Let’s go," he said.
They entered THE Maw, joined only by Andro, the other Source Lifeforms remaining behind at the mouth, and the dark closed over them as they descended.

Ambient hostility increasing with depth.
Environmental pressures and Pulse intensity rising.
Raging existential winds present, carrying the foreign converted nature; capable of cutting into the existence of any being whose Akashic Civilizational Intent is of insufficient rarity to ward it.

It tried to cut into all of them!
WUU!

WUU!

Towards... want!
Towards Loot!
His senses were tingling!
His foundations, steeped now in Infinity and THE Primordial Source, recognized something ahead and leaned toward it.

chapters.title: Chapter 5361: Upheaval! I
paragraphs: In the next instant, existence cracked!
Fissures erupted from the depths of THE Maw, racing up through the obsidian crystal and the abandoned scaffolding and the lethal dark, and it did not feel like stone breaking!

It felt like the fabric underneath the stone breaking, like the idea that held the mine together had developed a flaw and the flaw was spreading. And in the middle of that cracking, Noah felt something grand.
He felt THE Prime Cause of Bellum of Arkethys move.

Move, with purpose, the war-truth of an entire Observable Existence turning like a head turning, and it imposed itself, deliberately, onto Dame Seraphine and the other Fifth Scale existence present. The Cause of an Observable Existence does not choose targets...normally. It is a foundational truth, not a creature with intentions.
And yet this one chose, and it chose the strongest beings in the mine!
Something Noah had done...in Chernobyl!
HUUM!
Sir William moved first, and the other Swords moved with him.

They closed around Noah and Seo-yeon, Sir William and Botswana and Richard and Lianna placing themselves between the pair and the depths of THE Maw, a wall of Source Lifeforms with their Armaments drawn, because every one of them knew exactly how prized the man and the child were, and every one of them had been told in their own way that protecting them was the point of being here.
It was discipline, fast and total, four Titan-rarity Swords arranging themselves around the two beings an Order from THE Domicile had sent them to keep alive.

|Alert: An unknown foreign will has imposed itself upon this location. It is asserting authority not through any visible body but through THE Arkethys Observable Existence itself, commanding the domain’s Prime Causes as extensions of its intent.|
The moment the words bloomed in front of Noah, something erupted from the depths of THE Maw, and it shook every existence present down to its foundations.

It came as a singularity at first, a spinning point in the deep dark from which the Unstable Pulse had been echoing the whole time, the heart of the conversion, the thing that had been beating like a buried organ beneath the mine. It spun and it pulled and the foreign nature poured off it in waves. And then, in a moment, the singularity cleared, the spinning resolving into stillness, and at the very center of it, where the dark had been, there was a hand.
A hand, cleaved at the wrist.

It hung in the deep of THE Maw, decrepit and gray-blue, the skin drawn tight and dried over what was underneath, the cut at the wrist clean and ancient, a thing that had been severed from whatever it belonged to a very long time ago. By itself it might have looked like a relic. A dead thing. A grim curiosity dredged up from somewhere it should have stayed buried.
Then Noah focused on it, and what he saw stopped being grim and became something far worse.

The dried muscle of it. The bones beneath the muscle. Every separate piece of that cleaved hand radiated an aura so profound, so dense, so utterly beyond anything he had measured, thateach individual part of it, each withered finger, each ancient bone, exceeded Dame Seraphine!

Exceeded the other Fifth Scale existences. Exceeded every Mesozoic Scale being he had encountered since arriving in THE Source Lands. It was not a hand carrying a Fifth Scale aura. It was a hand whose every separate component was, on its own, more than a Fifth Scale being, and the hand was only a hand, only a piece, cleaved at the wrist from something that had once been whole!
It was horrid! To the extent he made a move right away!
He reached out and put his hand on Seo-yeon.

He did not explain. There was no time to explain, and the protective wall of Swords could not protect her from a thing whose fingers outweighed Dame Seraphine. So he brought the little girl into his existence and flung her through THE Infinite Cause that all his bodies shared, hurling her across the impossible distance between THE Maw and another of his bodies, the one waiting in THE Infiniverse, sending her out of this place and toward the safest location he owned in all of existence!
One breath she was on the edge of his perception. The next she was gone, away, somewhere the cleaved hand could not reach her.
And before he could do anything else, the hand moved!
BOOM!
|Existence declares that all spatial movements are restricted and locked down in this region for anything not given permission.|

The decrepit fingers tapped out, one after another, and it happened in what looked like slow motion and was not slow at all. The fingers seemed to drift, unhurried, ancient and patient, and yet they moved faster than any of them could track, faster than Noah’s perception could follow even sharpened as it was, the gap between the look of the motion and the speed of it a thing that made his foundations recoil.
Dame Seraphine roared.

Her body blazed with brilliant light, THE Mesozoic Scale being gathering herself to do something, to fight or to ward or to put herself between the hand and the new Sword.And in the very next instant, she was gone.

She and Andro both disappeared, displaced, flung elsewhere by the tapping of those fingers, removed from THE Maw entirely, not killed, not struck down, simply taken off the board, as though the cleaved hand had looked at the two Fifth Scale beings present and decided they were not worth the bother of dealing with directly.
It had moved them aside the way a person sweeps crumbs from a table before setting down something that matters!
The fingers turned toward Noah, and Sir William, and the other Swords!
And every one of them felt their existence anchored in place, pinned, held, by a power none of them had ever faced and none of them had a frame to understand.
It pressed down on all of them at once, the oppression of a thing that did not need to act to dominate, that simply existed nearby and made existing nearby an unbearable weight.
For Noah, it was heaviest of all!

He felt the hand’s attention settle on him specifically, the bulk of that profound and horrid oppression turning toward him and resting there, singling him out from the four Swords arrayed around where he stood. It had swept Dame Seraphine aside as an irrelevance. It had pinned the Swords as an afterthought. And it had chosen him, out of everyone in THE Maw, as the thing worth focusing on.

|ALARM: Information is being received from the surrounding existence. This information does not originate fully from me. The unknown Source is radiating its own weavings of information into the environment, weavings that constantly break and transform the Infinity and Primordial Source around them, forcing the surrounding existence to carry the message and act on what it wishes. This is communication enforced as conversion. The surroundings themselves are being made to speak on its behalf.|
|Received transmission:You are being observed by THE Sealed One. Kneel and let go. Kneel and let go. KNEEL AND LET GO. KNEEL! LET GO!|
BOOM!

The information was not information. It hit like a physical force, the weight of a will old enough and vast enough that its mere instruction carried the mass of an impact, and even Noah, who had never once gone to his knees, was smashed backward by it!
His body tore through the air of THE Maw, the oppression slamming into his existence with the words themselves, KNEEL, LET GO!
Around him, the Swords clutched their heads and roared.

Sir William. Botswana. Richard. Lianna. Four Titan-rarity Swords of Existence, beings who had faced apocalyptic Gilded forces and never bent, clutching their skulls as the transmission tore through them, and then, one after another, falling!
Oh!
To their knees!

Their bodies forced down by a will that converted resistance into compliance, their eyes wide and filled with incredulity and shock and a horror that none of them had worn before, kneeling in the dark of THE Maw before a cleaved gray-blue hand, while the surrounding existence screamed its single ancient instruction into all of them!
The same instruction!
KNEEL.
LET GO.

|ALARM: Information is being received from the surrounding existence.
This information does not originate fully from me.

The unknown Source is radiating its own weavings of information into the environment, weavings that constantly break and transform the Infinity and Primordial Source around them, forcing the surrounding existence to carry the message and act on what it wishes.
This is communication enforced as conversion.
The surroundings themselves are being made to speak on its behalf.|
|Received transmission:You are being observed by THE Sealed One.
Kneel and let go.
Kneel and let go.
KNEEL AND LET GO.
KNEEL!
LET GO!|
BOOM!
The information was not information.

It hit like a physical force, the weight of a will old enough and vast enough that its mere instruction carried the mass of an impact, and even Noah, who had never once gone to his knees, was smashed backward by it!
His body tore through the air of THE Maw, the oppression slamming into his existence with the words themselves, KNEEL, LET GO!
Around him, the Swords clutched their heads and roared.
Sir William.
Botswana.
Richard.
Lianna.

Four Titan-rarity Swords of Existence, beings who had faced apocalyptic Gilded forces and never bent, clutching their skulls as the transmission tore through them, and then, one after another, falling!
Oh!
To their knees!

Their bodies forced down by a will that converted resistance into compliance, their eyes wide and filled with incredulity and shock and a horror that none of them had worn before, kneeling in the dark of THE Maw before a cleaved gray-blue hand, while the surrounding existence screamed its single ancient instruction into all of them!
The same instruction!
KNEEL.
LET GO.

chapters.title: Chapter 5362: Upheaval! II
paragraphs: Noah hit the crystal wall of THE Maw, came off it without slowing, and reached for the Swords with the only thing he had that might help them as he saw them on their knees.
He did not want to lose this body here as he had to work with everyone while they grasped what they came across!

THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian erupted out of him, the obsidian gold flooding the dark of the mine, and he stretched it toward the four kneeling figures the way he had wrapped it around Seo-yeon against the Pulse.

If the cleaved hand was forcing them down through the converted Infinity and Primordial Source of their own bodies, then his Aura, with his identity forged unbreakable into its foundation, might give them something to hold to. Might wall their existences off from the will pressing them into the ground. It was worth trying!
The Swords felt it reach them, and they answered.

Sir William’s Titan Intent of dignity erupted first, the obsidian phantom of regality unfolding around him even as he knelt, the record of a being who had never once compromised his standards rising in defiance of a will that demanded he abandon them.
Botswana’s Wrathbound Bulwark blazed up beside it, the record of endured violence turned to refusal, a being who had survived everything insisting that he would survive this too.
He would survive as he always had!
Richard’s Lucid Aegis flared, his understanding fighting to see clearly through the conversion. Lianna’s Veiled Current turned, trying to slip her existence out of the grip that held it.
Four third-rarity Intents, four records of beings who had earned the right to impose themselves on existence, erupting together in the dark of THE Maw!
And the cleaved hand answered them with patience.
|Transmission received:Kneel and let go.|
|Kneel and let go, or the collapse of your peers will be on your hands. You are being given the choice. Be grateful for the courtesy and kneel.|
The words landed inside Noah’s existence with the weight of the thing that spoke them, and they were not a bluff!
He answered it anyway.
Him? Fucking kneel?!
"No," Noah said, and roared it into the dark. "NO!"
He pulled.

He reached into THE Infinite Cause, the Cause that backed two Observable Existences, and dragged its full weight up into himself. He reached into his Einherjar Source, the bastion-heavy third Demarcation with Hamingja running golden through it, and called on the grand luck that bent surrounding existence to favor him!

He reached across THE Undefined Gaps to the body that pulled the immensity of THE Infiniverse on its shoulders, and he drew on that immensity too, the weight of an entire Observable Existence channeled toward the hand. He gathered everything he was, every authority, every body, every Cause, and turned it on the cleaved gray-blue thing hanging in the deep of THE Maw, because he was not going to kneel, and he was going to pull those four beings out of the ground if it could be done at all!
What happened next...occurred in the span of a single instant.

The decrepit fingers turned toward the Swords coldly and the converted Infinity and Primordial Source that composed the four Swords twisted, all at once, turning against the existences they belonged to, the authorities of their own bodies bending toward a will that was not theirs.
It was horrifying as they were all...very clearly outmatched. Their records and knowledge...felt like a tiny boat while that hand felt like a vast, tumultuous sea.
All of them here felt an unfathomably heavy foreboding sensation!
All of them felt their Sources begin to shiver and tremble! Why...why would their sources be trembling?
Botswana’s roar changed in his throat.

The great scarred titan who had laughed and called Noah brother fought it, his Wrathbound Bulwark surging, his whole record of endured survival thrown against the thing unmaking him from the inside, and for a moment the moment held, the titan straining, Noah’s Aura wrapped around him, the two of them pushing back against the collapse together!

Then the converted authority of his body wrenched around, dragged him to face Noah, made his expression into something to be looked at, and his eyes found the new Sword across the dark, wide and disbelieving, the eyes of a being who had always assumed he would die fighting and could not understand why the fight was being taken from him.
His existence and his Source came apart.
Unraveled by a power he, a Triassic Scale Existence, could not deny.

What had been a titan became a river of crimson-tinged light, flowing across the dark of THE Maw and into the cleaved hand, which glowed crimson as it drank him down. Noah’s Aura closed on the space where he had been and found nothing left to hold.
"Botswana!"

Richard howled in rage and pain as was already going. The small quick Sword who had paced and theorized and enjoyed his own cleverness fought it the only way he knew how, his Lucid Aegis straining to understand the mechanism even as the mechanism took him, and his bright darting eyes were forced to look at Noah as if a massive invisible hand forced them to.
And in them was a terrible final clarity, the clarity of a being who had at last seen the whole shape of the thing and understood, too late, that it was too grand.
His face was turned toward Noah as...
BOOM! CRACK!
A Pulse tore through him. His existence came apart. He became a river, and the river was drunk, and the hand glowed brighter.
Lianna’s existence buzzed!
The woman who gave nothing away gave nothing away even now, her Veiled Current twisting, trying to slip her existence sideways out of a grip that had no sideways to slip toward!
Her Akashic Civilizational Intent was grand!
Her record was heavy!
But...it seemed like it held nothing compared to the record of that decrepit hand!
It failed to stand!
And when it failed, her head was forcefully turned as she met Noah’s eyes with something that was almost an apology and almost a warning and was gone before he could read which it had been.
Her face was shown to him. Her existence came apart. The river flowed. The hand drank!
And then there was Sir William.

The Gentleman Knight was the last left kneeling, his Titan Intent of dignity still burning around him, the obsidian phantom of regality flickering as the converted authority of his own body turned against the existence it composed.

Noah threw everything he had left toward him, the full weight of the Aura and the Infinite Cause and THE Infiniverse, reaching for his sponsor, the being who had vouched for him and given him the path, the one whose collapse he was not going to allow if collapse could be refused!
And yet...
Oh, and yet...
It could not be refused. He felt it. He felt the same thing he had felt with the other three, the absolute insufficiency of everything he was against the thing in the dark!
The other three had their faces turned to Noah against their will. Sir William turned his own!

He looked at Noah of his own choosing, his composure unbroken even as his existence began to come apart around it, even as the dignity of an entire life burned down toward its final ember, and he held the one thing that no power could take from a being unless the being handed it over.
"Persevere," Sir William said.
His voice was steady. It had no right to be steady. His existence was unraveling around the word and his voice did not shake!
"If you can do nothing else." The phantom of regality dimmed, guttered. "In the face of the impossible, Persevere."
HUUM!
A breath, the last of his composure, spent on purpose. "Manners...Maketh...Man."
BOOM!
His existence came apart as he Akashic Civilizational Intent was shredded to oblivion.

He became a river of light, dignified even in the shape of his unmaking, and the river flowed across the dark of THE Maw and into the cleaved hand, and the hand glowed crimson and full and turned, at last, to Noah, alone now over four absences where his companions had been.
|Transmission received: That... could have been avoided.|
|Remember that I offered, and you refused, and they paid. Kneel and let go, and the next ones you care for will not have to.|

Noah stood in the dark, four rivers of the dead glowing crimson inside a cleaved gray-blue hand, and the rage that moved through him was the clean cold rage of a being who had just been taught something he would never forgive.
It had killed them to make a point.
It thought that would bend him!
It had read him wrong!
The hand shot toward him.

And Noah bellowed, a sound that came up out of everything he was, the roar of a being who had stood before Dame Seraphine’s pressure and refused, who had stood in his own father’s illusion and refused, and who would stand here, in the dark, over the rivers of the dead, and refuse again.
He would always refuse!

THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian blazed to its absolute height, obsidian gold flooding THE Maw until the crystal walls and the abandoned scaffolding and the cleaved hand itself were all lit by the immensity of it, the nine Prime Causes burning across its surface, THE Infinite Cause and THE Einherjar Source and the weight of THE Infiniverse all pouring through him at once, an emperor’s defiance roaring!
Roaring!
The hand pierced through all of it.

It pierced the Aura, pierced the light, pierced every authority he had raised against it, the decrepit gray-blue fingers passing through the immensity of THE Source Barbarian as though the immensity were a curtain, and it drove toward his chest, toward the center of his existence, toward the place where his identity sat forged into the foundation of his Infinity.
Seeking to enter him!

chapters.title: Chapter 5363: Upheaval! III
paragraphs: There is a thought people like to comfort themselves with.
The unstoppable force meets the immovable object, and existence holds its breath to see which one gives, and the question is supposed to be grand and unanswerable and a little bit beautiful.
It is a nice thought.
It belongs to beings who have only ever met forces and objects.
Because somewhere above the unstoppable and the immovable both, older than the framing of the question, there are things that do not care for the contest at all.

Things that were ancient when the first force learned to push and the first object learned to hold. Things that look at the grand unanswerable question the way an adult looks at two children arguing over which of them is stronger, and that reach down, without much interest, and pick the argument up, and end it, because the argument was never theirs and the children were never anything but small.
The decrepit hand was one of those things.
And so it met almost no resistance.

The power it held was so far beyond the framing of force and object that THE Aura of THE Source Barbarian, the established expression of everything Noah was, was simply being pushed aside. Not broken. Not overpowered in any contest that deserved the name.
Moved, the way a hand moves a curtain it intends to walk through, the gigaparsec-grade authority of THE Source Barbarian set gently and absolutely out of the way.
And at that moment, with the hand passing through everything he had ever built, Noah bellowed in defiance.

He looked like an ancient fiend dragged up out of some buried age, his mentality gone cold and callous and clear, the specific clarity of a being who has stopped feeling fear because fear has nothing left to offer him!

His entire body, his skin, began to shine with multicolored jade-like brilliance, the Infinity and THE Primordial Source surfacing through him until he looked less like a man and more like some ancient treasure unearthed from a place that should have stayed sealed!

And behind him, summoned by the crisis of their own volition, the illusory manifestations of Ruination and THE Infiniverse bloomed into being in boundless multicolored Infinity, both of them roaring, both of them furious, two beings who had never been afraid for him before!

Ruination’s churning Infinity lines surged forward and pressed her hands flat against Noah’s back, pouring everything she was into bracing him. THE Infiniverse drew back an illusory spear of boundless multicolored Infinity, and struck, the spear passing straight through Noah’s own form to drive at the decrepit hand reaching for his chest, an entire Observable Existence throwing its weight behind a single thrust to protect the man it answered to!
HUUUM!
The hand showed something that might, on an ancient and decrepit thing, have been surprise.
It was not surprise for long.

In the next moment, seas appeared behind the cleaved fingers. Boundless Primordial Source and boundless Infinity, vast beyond reckoning, and the two of them were not held apart the way every being in the current age held them apart.
They were melded together, tightly, in an ancient and seamless manner, fused into a single thing the way nothing in this age could fuse them, and that fused sea pushed.
The spear of THE Infiniverse, the thrust of an entire Observable Existence, was decimated instantly. The boundless crystalline jade brilliance across Noah’s skin was torn away.

And the hand drove on, into him, the gray-blue fingers tearing through his Hadean skin and into the musculature beneath it, through the Osmontian Infinite musculature and into the bones beneath that, through the nine Prime Cause marrow channels and the Infinite meridians and the nerves, parting the entire terrifying architecture of his body that had been forged across apocalypses.

It pierced all of it. Skin, muscle, bone, the whole foundation that had withstood the weight of two Observable Existences in THE Undefined Gaps, and it arrived in his chest cavity, and there, at last, going through that much,the decrepit hand finally showed a sense of tiredness.
It was noticeably weaker now. The passage had cost it something. Tearing through a foundation like Noah’s, even for a thing that sat above forces and objects, was not free.
But its job was done. It was in!

And once inside, surging toward his multicolored heart, it almost hesitated, because it saw how much there was. So many organs. So many systems. THE Osmontian Organ of Existence producing Observable and Unobservable Force, the marrow channels, the meridians, the whole impossible interior of a being who had built himself into something no framework accounted for!

For a moment the hand seemed to face the difficulty of choice, spoiled by the sheer abundance of foundation to plunge into, like a thief who breaks into a vault and finds it too full to know what to take first.
In the end, it chose decisively.
It went for the heart.

Weakened, tired, having spent more than it expected on the passage in, but in, and closing on the multicolored heart at the center of everything Noah was, and its transmission rolled out domineering and patient and almost gentle.
|Transmission received: I will take good care of your body.|

|From the moment you arrived in this place, the pull from you has been intoxicating. I did not think a foundation like this could still exist in these times. I had given up expecting it. And there is so much more you are hiding, I can feel it, layers and layers you have not shown anyone. It is all right. It is over now. Stop fighting. It is over now.|
HUUM!
Inside his own body, Noah roared.
And at that moment, boundless seas of Osmontian Absolute Infinity surged up from the depths of his existence and rushed toward his heart, not to attack the hand, but to wrap. To contain!

He poured his identity-forged Infinity around his own multicolored heart in compressed layers, wrapping it again and again and again, and he did it with a structure pulled from the deepest weavings he knew, folding the Infinity around his heart the way a Calabi-Yau manifold folds dimension into dimension, layer within layer within layer, infinite restriction packed into finite space, a prison whose walls turned back on themselves endlessly so that the thing inside could never find an edge to push against!

He was not trying to kill it. He had understood, somewhere in the cold clarity, that he could not kill it. So he did the only thing left to the desperate and the very clever, the same thing its own jailers had done to whatever it had been cleaved from. He could not destroy it. So he would seal it!

|An extremely powerful foreign influence has breached all defenses and entered the heart. It continues to impose a terrifying influence, seeking to alter and control your Infinity and your Primordial Source, to convert your foundation toward its own nature and take your body as its own. Direct destruction is not possible. The influence exceeds all measure available to me.|

|Containment in progress. You are wrapping the foreign influence in compressed, self-folding layers of Osmontian Absolute Infinity, a restriction with no accessible edge, exploiting the manifold structure to deny it any surface to push against.|

|Critical factor: The foreign influence is weakened. The passage through your Osmontian architecture cost it more than it anticipated. The strength of your foundation, the bracing of my Everything, and the strike of THE Infiniverse have reduced its power below its full expression. The reduction may be sufficient. The reduction may be just barely sufficient. Continue wrapping. Do not stop. Do not stop. The Osmontian Absolute Infinity is the last defense and it must hold against something neither of us can fully understand, so you must hold it, you must hold, you must hold, you must hol—|
BOOM!
The Infinity raged, layer folding over layer over layer, his identity thrown around the foreign thing as the final wall between himself and a fluency that had eaten beings since before THE Scales!
And then, everything went dark.
